articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Extraction Methods for Stray Inductance Based on Double Pulse Testing Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The stray inductance of commutating current paths significantly affects the test results in Double Pulse Test (DPT) of Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBT). Thus, precise calculation of stray inductance is crucial for assessing the device performance in DPT. In this study, we firstly analyze the switching transient process of DPT circuits. Then, five typical methods including the traditional differential, polynomial fitting, whole switching process differential, integral and frequency-domain methods are used to extract the stray inductance. To optimize the calculation of current change rate, we further propose an enhanced differential method by employing Sliding Discrete Fourier Transform (SDFT). Finally, the accuracy and practicality of these methods are verified and compared with the Q3D simulation results.

articleTitle: The Impact of Harmonics on the D- and Q- Axis Inductance of Permanent Magnet Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper analyzes the direct and quadrature axis inductance of permanent magnet synchronous motors based on the non-power invariant transformation in Park’s transformation. Considering coupling and high-order harmonics, a mathematical model of the stator winding of the permanent magnet synchronous motor is established, and the expressions of the d- and q- axis inductance of the motor are analytically calculated and compared with the equivalent inductance. The accuracy of the calculation is verified by finite element simulation, using both transient and static magnetic field methods.

Author Keywords: Calculation of D- and Q- Axis Inductance

articleTitle: An accurate BiLSTM data-driven model for SOH prediction of lithium batteries based on health indicators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Accurate state of health (SOH) is a key indicator to evaluate the lifespan of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, complex nonlinear capacity degradation and unmeasurable internal chemical reactions pose great challenges to accurate SOH estimation of LIBs. Therefore, this article proposed a novel bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) data-driven model to further improve the precision of battery SOH prediction. First, The incremental capacity (IC) curve was obtained by the battery aging cycle test. Subsequently, the health factors related to SOH were extracted from the IC curve. Moreover, the health indicators are taken as the input to the BiLSTM model, and the calculated SOH is the output of the model. Finally, the BiLSTM model was trained by the CS2-36 battery dataset provided by the CALCE team and the model prediction accuracy was verified by another CS2-37 battery dataset. The results indicate that the mean absolute error (MAE) of the proposed BiLSTM data-driven model is kept within 1%. Moreover, the root mean square error (RMSE) was reduced by 18.4% and 48.8%, respectively, compared with the gated recurrent unit (GRU) and LSTM model.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Method for Health Monitoring of Lithium-Ion Batteries in Real-World Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Accurate and efficient monitoring of the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries during operation is the key to ensure the safe and reliable operation of electric vehicles (EVs). However, applying existing lab-based methods directly to field data is challenging due to the complex operating conditions in realistic scenarios. Therefore, this study introduces a data-driven SOH estimation method tailored for real-world applications. The proposed method begins by utilizing the ampere-hour integral to calculate the SOH label based on the charging data. Statistical analysis and an unsupervised learning algorithm are then employed to screen the SOH label and ensure its rationality. Next, statistical features are extracted from the charging data, and health indicator sets are selected using two correlation analysis methods: Pearson correlation and grayscale correlation. Subsequently, a machine learning regression algorithm is applied, using the optimized feature set, to establish the SOH estimation model. To verify the effectiveness of this approach, field data from approximately one year of operation for 200 EVs is used. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate SOH estimation, with the mean absolute error of less than 2.02%.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Adjustable Capability of Virtual Power Plants Considering the Dynamic Aggregation of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) can be aggregated into virtual power plants (VPPs) to participate in grid scheduling. However, due to the mobility of EVs, estimating their adjustable capability is highly stochastic. Therefore, this paper proposes a method to characterize the adjustable capability of VPPs considering the dynamic aggregation of EVs. Firstly, a VPP layering and partition strategy is proposed, combining grid structure and administrative divisions to layer and partition the adjustable capability of flexible resources. Subsequently, the dynamic characteristics of the EV aggregation process are analyzed in detail. The adjustable capability of EVs aggregated into VPPs is characterized using a time-varying confidence interval estimation method. Based on actual data from 18,000 charging stations in Shanghai, this paper reveals their daily cycle characteristics and evaluates the regulation potential of EVs in different times and regions, with simulation verification conducted using MATLAB.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Optimization of Tangential Rotor for a Low-Speed High-Torque Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: For low-speed high-torque permanent magnet motors, the rotor types of the motor are primarily categorized into two main varieties: the interior permanent magnet rotor and the surface-mounted rotor. However, there is still a lack of research on the tangential rotor in the field of low speed and high torque. In this paper, a comprehensive analysis of the interior tangential rotor is carried out in a 1200 kW, 75rpm low speed permanent magnet motor. The analysis of this paper covers various aspects such as the amount of permanent magnets, efficiency, motor length, power factor, torque, etc. Firstly, the initial design parameters of 1200 kW 75 rpm low speed permanent magnet motor are determined by finite element analysis. On this basis, the electromagnetic optimization scheme of the interior tangential rotor is proposed. Finally, the performance of the interior tangential rotor is compared and analyzed in detail, and a prototype is made to verify the theoretical analysis. In general, this paper provides practical guidance and reference for the design of low-speed permanent magnet motor, and promotes the progress of motor technology.

articleTitle: A Cascaded H -Bridge Converter With Staggered Phase-shifting Transformer for Cruise Ship Shore-based Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Shore-based frequency power supply system have been widely used to solve the problem of air pollution caused by ships at ports. However, theoretical and engineering research on cruise ship shore-based power system is not yet sufficient.This paper presents a CHB topology for cruise ship shore-based frequency power system. The input transformer adopts two parallel phase-shifting transformers with epoxy casting structure.The Primary and secondary edges of each one are staggered and form 60 pulses rectification. An energy absorption circuit is developed for the power module to absorb the reverse power when the ship is connected to the shore grid. A high-voltage LC filter is also designed on the output side. It solves the problems of high voltage, difficulty in increasing the capacity, low THD and large volume of the converter. The single 16MVA frequency converter has been developed in a cruise ship port in China. Currently, it is the largest shore-based frequency power supply system in Asia. Moreover, the operating principle, mathematical model, and control strategy are presented. Finally,the method proposed in this paper has been tested by industrial site. The test and application results prove the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Investigation of Constant Power Output Capability on Reverse Salient Consequent Pole PM Machine for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Permanent magnet (PM) synchronous machines (PMSMs) have been widely used in electric vehicle (EV) drives because of their high torque/power density and high efficiency. To meet the requirement of high-speed operation for EV applications, a common control method of the negative d-axis current is employed to reduce the air-gap magnetic field, which may result in irreversible demagnetization risk of the PMs. To achieve a constant-power operation capability in high-speed conditions, a new reverse salient consequent-pole PM (RSCPPM) machine is proposed and developed with consequent-pole rotor design, which is characterized by multiple rotor flux barriers and hence resulting a higher d-axis inductance than q-axis inductance. Subsequently, the influence of key parameters, including the split ratio, PM width, rotor flux barrier width, and different load currents, on the flux weakening coefficient of the proposed RSCPPM machines are investigated by the finite element (FE) method. Lastly, experiment results on the RSCPPM prototype were conducted, and the tested results matched well with the FE simulations.

articleTitle: Research on Factors Influencing Carbon Emission Intensity of Wharf Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: As an important node of world trade, ports connect the landing side logistics chain with maritime transportation. Reducing the carbon emissions of wharf structure is of importance in maritime transportation. In order to analyze the key factors affecting the carbon emissions, we calculate the carbon emissions in the construction period, which has the highest carbon emissions in the whole life cycle of wharf structure. In this paper, we firstly calculate several actual projects based on existing carbon emission calculation models, including gravity structure and high pile structure, which are the two most common forms of wharf structure. Then, by selecting the carbon emissions per unit surface area of the structure as the standard, we proposed a carbon emission calculation model applicable to wharfs with different structural forms. finally, we obtain the key factors of carbon emissions during the construction period of wharf project through sensitivity analysis. Experimental results show that the carbon emissions of building materials are higher than 70%, and that of high pile wharf is higher than 90%. Additionally, the carbon emissions of wharf structure are positively correlated with the wharf tonnage, and the carbon emissions of gravity structure is more sensitive to the change of tonnage.

articleTitle: Joint Estimation of Battery Core Temperature and Convection Coefficient Based on Efficient Thermal Model Using Two-parameter Approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Accurate and efficient estimation of the battery core temperature is essential for the reliable and safe battery system. However, restricted by the current sensing and testing technologies, it is challenging to directly measure the core temperature of the lithium-ion battery. Furthermore, due to the time-varying convection coefficient and the limited on-board computational resource, it is difficult to accurately estimate the battery core temperature in real-time. Consequently, this paper proposes a joint estimation method for the convection coefficient and the core temperature of the lithium-ion battery based on an efficient thermal model. Specifically, considering the computational cost and the estimation accuracy, a two-parameter polynomial approximation method is employed to reduce the model order, and the dual extended Kalman filter algorithm is utilized to simultaneously estimate the core temperature and the convection coefficient of the battery. The validation results show that the proposed method can accurately and quickly predict the core temperature under unknown cooling conditions, and the root mean square error is less than 1°C.

articleTitle: Optimization Design Of PMSM With High Torque Density and Large Overload
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In order to improve the torque density and overload performance of permanent magnet synchronous motor, the electromagnetic analysis of the motor is carried out from the topological level. Firstly, the effects of pole-slot combination on the torque density and overload performance of the motor are analyzed respectively. Then, according to the Halbach structure, the effect of different block number and width of each pole on the motor torque density and overload performance is analyzed. Finally, on the basis of the above research, three kinds of motor topologies with better performance are selected to provide guidance for the follow-up research work.

articleTitle: Research on thermal characteristics of LED vehicle light module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Owing to numerous advantages of high luminous efficiency, good monochromaticity, and rich colors, light-emitting diodes (LEDs) have been widely used in vehicle lighting. However, the enclosed operation environment has brought a high temperature scenario for LED vehicle lights (LED-VLs) during operation. This results in the reduction of luminous efficiency and lifespan. It is of great importance to achieve excellent thermal management for the LED-VL by reducing its operation temperature to guarantee long-term and stable operation. In this study, a vapor chamber (VC) was proposed to achieve effective thermal management for a LED-VL module by significantly reducing the temperature of LEDs. The temperature characteristics of a LED-VL module without VC were investigated by combining simulation and experimental verification. The effectiveness of using VC for thermal management of a LED-VL module was validated. Results indicate that the LED unit exhibits a high temperature of 73.7 °C, which is in good agreement with the testing data. This study verifies that the introduction of VC can help reduce the temperature of the LED-VL module for practical use.

articleTitle: Analysis and Reduction of Detent Force on a Novel Transverse Flux Permanent Magnet Linear Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Due to the influence of end effect, the air-gap magnetic density at both ends is seriously distorted, which results in high detent force. In this paper, a typical transverse flux permanent magnet linear machine (TFLM) is introduced to analyze the detent force in depth. The detent force of permanent magnet linear machines is composed of both end force and cogging force. It can be better analyzed and suppressed by separating the cogging effect from end effect. By using the proportional separation method, the end force and cogging force of TFLM are separately analyzed. By virtual displacement method, the influencing factors of cogging force are investigated. According to Maxwell tensor method, the variation law of end force is solved. To reduce the detent force of TFLM, the axial length of end boot is optimized, and the unequal-width boot and auxiliary pole are proposed. Finally, the proposed methods of reducing the detent force are validated to be effective by 3-D finite element simulation.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control of SPMSMs Based on Nonlinear Flux Model and High Frequency Voltage Injection Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: For the sensorless control of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motors (SPMSMs), the traditional pulsating high frequency square wave injection method exhibits poor position estimation accuracy under low-speed overload conditions, mainly due to neglecting the cross-coupling effects and nonlinear parameter variations of motor inductances in classical control models. To address this issue, this paper proposes a high-frequency injection method based on a nonlinear flux model. Firstly, a high-frequency square wave voltage signal is injected into the stator winding, and a high-frequency current response signal is separated. Then, the envelope of the high-frequency current response undergoes vector cross multiplication to compensate for terms related to cross-coupling effects. Finally, the position information of the rotor is obtained through the phase-locked loop. This paper also compares the traditional pulsating high frequency square wave injection method, the source of position estimation error and the reason of ‘salient pole failure’ are analyzed. Both simulation and experimental results validate the proposed method, which is simple and reliable, effectively reducing position estimation errors of SPMSMs under low-speed overload conditions.

Author Keywords: pulsating high frequency square wave injection method

articleTitle: Design of Active EMI Filter for CM EMI Suppression with Cascaded Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In power electronic equipment, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is an important issue to ensure the reliable operation of the system. The performance of the electromagnetic interference (EMI) filters is critical to the EMC characteristics of the equipment. For the passive EMI filter which is used as the primary method for EMI suppression, its performance can be improved by cascading other passive EMI filters and a similar method can be used in the active EMI filter (AEF) which is composed of active components. In this paper, a current-sensing current-compensating AEF with cascaded structure for common mode (CM) EMI suppression is proposed. The CM EMI suppression effect of the cascaded AEF is verified by experiment, and it can suppress CM EMI better than the single stage AEF.

articleTitle: Intelligent Parameter Identification of PMSM Based on BPNN Fitting Nonlinear Relationships
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, an intelligent parameter identification algorithm of the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is proposed. Firstly, a high-fidelity motor parameter model considering cross coupling effects is constructed using a polynomial model to accurately describe the magnetic saturation scenario, which is difficult to achieve with traditional motor equations. Secondly, an improved- backpropagation neural network (BPNN) is used to identify the coefficients in this model by fitting explicit time-domain relationships, effectively avoiding a large amount of direct calculations. In this framework, the accurate identification of multi-dimensional parameters is realized by changing the definition of loss function, combining backpropagation and making full use of the nonlinear fitting ability of neural network. Finally, Simulations and experiments verify the accuracy and convergence speed of parameter identification.

articleTitle: Long-Horizon PMSM Model Predictive Speed Control Based on Laguerre Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Speed control represents an important component in servo systems. Conventional speed control strategy based on Proportional-Integral (PI) control cannot simultaneously optimize response speed and control precision. To enhance the speed control performance of servo control systems, the article proposes a novel Laguerre functions Long-Horizon Model Predictive Speed Control strategy. The algorithm adopts an incremental speed prediction model, selects Laguerre basis functions to represent the control signal, and derives the optimal control signal through the resolution of a cost function. Furthermore, considering the current constraint of the motor, the quadratic programming problem can solve the final control signal. Finally, Experimental validation of the proposed method shows its effectiveness and feasibility compared to conventional cascaded PI control.

articleTitle: A Multi-functional Integrated Motor-Driving and Onboard-Charging System Based on Three-Motor-Drive Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Due to the non-renewable nature of fossil energy sources, the popularity of electric vehicles has become a trend. Meanwhile, the need for battery charging is a very important part of electric vehicles (EV) promotion. In this paper, a multifunctional integrated motor-driving and onboard-charging (IMDOC) system is proposed based on a three-motor-drive EV. In the proposed system, a five-phase flux-switching permanent-magnet (FSPM) motor and two three-phase FSPM motor are employed as the front and rear driving motor respectively in the driving mode. While in the charging mode, the system can be reconfigured to provide single/three-phase AC and DC charging capabilities at varying power levels. By reasonably combining the three motors and configuring the windings, the system can solve the problems of traditional IMDOC system and meet different charging needs. The effectiveness of the proposed IMDOC system is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Vehicle-to-Grid Loads Simulation and Prediction Considering Microscopic Traffic Behaviors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of technology and growing global awareness of environmental issues, the demand for electric vehicles (EVs) and other new energy vehicles (NEVs) has been increasing at an unprecedented rate. This surge has heightened the requirements for optimized charging load. However, a notable limitation in current research lies in its predominant focus on broad, macro-level traffic flow models. These models often struggle to accurately represent fine-grained simulations of individual vehicles and frequently overlook the application of vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology. These limitations hamper the safe operation of the power grid and the efficient utilization of resources. Therefore, by incorporating the application of V2G and employing refined simulation models, this research aims to replicate the charging patterns of electric vehicles within a realistic grid setting, thereby delving into the V2G load simulation. Furthermore, this paper proposes the utilization of deep learning model to fit and predict the V2G loads from data generated by refined traffic flow simulations. Integrating deep learning techniques is expected to significantly reduce simulation time while improving the performance and usability of the simulation results. This approach is designed to provide reliable technical support and assurance for the widespread adoption of electric vehicles in the future.

articleTitle: Selective ensemble learning enables battery capacity estimation across charging rates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Accurate and robust capacity estimation is crucial for battery health management. Data-driven methods for battery capacity estimation have demonstrated significant application value. However, optimal models evaluated during the offline training phase exhibit substantial variations across different estimation cases. This leads to the unstable performance of single data-driven models on unseen test cases. Moreover, these models often require costly retraining when the battery's charging current changes. To address these issues, this paper proposes a selective ensemble learning (SEL) method for online capacity estimation across varying charging rates. Seven health features, extracted from segment charging data, indicate the battery's aging behavior under different charging currents. A non-negative least squares regression model is used as a meta-learner to selectively integrate eight heterogeneous machine learning models. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an average capacity estimation error of 0.99% across three batteries with different charging rates. Comparative results reveal that the proposed method outperforms the best single machine learning model by 12.4% and significantly exceeds several advanced ensemble learning methods and deep learning methods by over 10%. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can enhance battery capacity estimation performance while reducing ensemble complexity. This research highlights the substantial potential of applying selective ensemble learning to battery capacity estimation in complex charging scenarios.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on the Characteristics of SiC FET/Si IGBT and SiC MOSFET/Si IGBT Hybrid Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The Si/SiC hybrid switch, which combines high power Si IGBTs with low power SiC MOSFETs, is considered an effective solution for reducing costs and improving efficiency. However, due to defects in the gate oxide layer of SiC MOSFETs, their gate voltage is not compatible with that of Si IGBTs. SiC FETs manufactured by UnitedSiC are a new type of silicon carbide device with low on-resistance and excellent switching performance. Compared to SiC MOSFETs, SiC FETs offer higher electron mobility and a more robust gate oxide. Additionally, their gate voltage is compatible with that of traditional Si IGBTs. Therefore, this paper proposes a SiC FET/Si IGBT hybrid switch, which provides a selective scheme for hybrid switch. The static and dynamic characteristics of the SiC FET/Si IGBT and SiC MOSFET/Si IGBT hybrid switches were compared under identical test conditions. Experimental results indicate that SiC FET/Si IGBT hybrid switches exhibit lower forward conduction voltage drop and reduced switching losses, making them more suitable for high switching frequency applications. The optimal turn-off delay of SiC MOSFET/Si IGBT hybrid switches exhibits low temperature sensitivity.

articleTitle: Research on EV charging load response management method based on short-term prediction results
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: An electrical vehicle (EV) charging load response management method based on short-term load forecasting results is proposed and discussed in this paper. Firstly, each user in the region makes an online reservation for their respective desired charging time and charging duration. And then, based on the signals submitted by all EVs in the region, the suggested charging start time for each EV is differentiated by considering the status of the EV's battery, the short-term forecasts of the charging load, and the response management objectives. After receiving the suggested time pushed by the system, each EV can voluntarily choose whether to accept the response management strategy or not. The proposed method fully coordinates the system optimization operation of the distribution network and EV charging behavior management. And the driver's participation is fully considered in the short-term EV charging load demand-side response process. The proposed method provides an important basic support for the system-level demand-side response regulation in the long-time scale.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method for the Rotating Components of Aircraft Multi-stage Brushless Synchronous Starter-Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: With the rapid development of the more electric aircraft (MEA) equipped with an integrated starter-generator, it is of great significance to carry out research on fault diagnosis of the multi-stage brushless synchronous starter-generator (MBSSG) to improve the reliability and maintainability of the system. An electrical fault diagnosis method for the rotating components of MBSSG based on the rotor currents of the main exciter (ME) is proposed in this paper. Through detailed analysis of the average values and averaged absolute values of the ME rotor currents under various fault conditions, electrical faults in the rotor of the ME, the rotating rectifier and the rotor of the main machine of the MBSSG can be detected and located. Simulation results verified the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Modeling of capacity attenuation of large capacity lithium iron phosphate batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: As the market demand for energy storage systems grows, large-capacity lithium iron phosphate (LFP) energy storage batteries are gaining popularity in electrochemical energy storage applications. Studying the capacity attenuation rules of these batteries under different conditions is crucial. This study establishes a one-dimensional lumped parameter model of a single lithium-ion battery to obtain its electrical characteristics. Simulation results demonstrate that the lumped parameter model can accurately simulate battery characteristics while disregarding factors like battery material and size, striking a balance between speed and accuracy. Based on this model, a semi-empirical and semi-physical capacity decay model, considering calendar life and cycle life, is developed. Key aging parameters necessary for the model are fitted based on a small amount of measured lithium-ion battery aging data, enabling the prediction of aging patterns of LFP batteries.

articleTitle: Modeling and Application of Meteorological-Transportation-Power Coupling Complex Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The transportation energy integration system comprises various interconnected monitoring variables that form a dynamic coupling relationship network, reflecting the system’s operational status. To address these issues, a coupled complex dynamic network integrating meteorological, transportation, and electricity factors is proposed. This approach first analyzes the causal relationship between meteorological conditions and traffic impedance using graph neural networks. Then, it converts the power consumption of electric vehicles into voltage sensitivity analysis of distribution power system nodes through an improved linear power-voltage model. Finally, the distribution power system nodes’ capacity to support the number of electric vehicles is determined. The results demonstrate that the proposed meteorological-transportation power coupling network effectively explores the interdependencies within these complex coupling networks, and its effectiveness is validated by practical cases.

articleTitle: A Novel SVPWM Scheme for Modular Multi Converter with Submodule Capacitor Voltage Balance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Space vector pulsewidth modulation (SVPWM) has good dc-link voltage utilization, but the determination of location of reference voltage vector and nearest three vectors will be complex in modular multi converter (MMC). This paper presents a novel SVPWM scheme with submodule capacitor voltage balance for MMC. The proposed method provides a general a determination of position for reference voltage vector and simplifies the computation without complicated trigonometric function. Finally, Simulation results demonstrate its validity.

articleTitle: Research on Composite Cooling and Heat Dissipation for Automotive Drive Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, for the cooling problem of high-power density automotive permanent magnet synchronous motors, the heat dissipation performance of the three structures of water-cooled, oil-cooled and oil-water composite cooling, and their effects on the performance of the motor are studied. By analyzing the loss distribution of the motor, the heat dissipation performance of different cooling structures under each working condition is calculated, and the maximum output capacity of the motor under the optimal cooling method is explored. The results show that the oil-water composite cooling structure can significantly reduce the motor temperature and improve the heat dissipation ability of the motor, thus increasing the peak power and peak torque of the motor. Under the oil-water composite cooling method, the peak power of the motor can be increased to 427.7kW and the peak torque can be increased to 384.8Nm, which are increased by 13.8% and 9.8% respectively. This shows that the oil-water composite cooling structure not only improves motor performance, but also has the potential to further miniaturize the motor. This study provides an important reference for the design of cooling systems for high-power density permanent magnet motors.

articleTitle: An Improved Current Sensorless Model Predictive Control for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Traditional permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive controller usually needs at least two phase current sensors to obtain feedback current to achieve high-precision control. However, this method not only increases the cost, but also may affect the reliability of the system due to the failure of the current sensor. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a control method of PMSM drive system without current sensor. In this method, the sliding mode observer (SMO) is used to estimate the dq-axes current, and the stability of the observer is analyzed by Lyapunov stability theorem, thus successfully eliminating the dependence on the current sensor. Through simulation research, this paper compares the control performance of current predictive control method with current sensor and without current sensor. The results show that the proposed method is comparable to the traditional current sensor method in control performance.

articleTitle: Insights into the Multi Physical Fields Coupling in Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells: Modeling and Numerical Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Durability issues have become the main obstacle to the commercialization process of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), especially for large area PEMFCs, it is important and challenging to obtain in-plane consistency information of PEMFCs quickly and accurately. In this paper, a three-dimensional (3D) multi physical fields coupling model of PEMFCs is proposed and developed. Specifically, a 3D model of current density and temperature coupling is developed. Additionally, the current density and temperature distributions in the PEMFC are numerically investigated. Furthermore, the analysis and insights into the mechanism behind the current density and temperature distributions are presented. The numerical results demonstrate that the proposed 3D multi physical fields coupling model achieves effective characterization, and can accurately display the distribution information of current density and temperature within the plane of PEMFCs. The developed 3D coupling model can provide a more economical and rapid reference for analyzing heterogeneity issues within PEMFCs, revealing significant potential in their application.

articleTitle: Voltage Error Compensation Strategy for High-Speed SRM Drives using Five-Segment Switching Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: To address the problem of output voltage lag in switched reluctance motors (SRM) drives caused by the discrete modulation mode, This paper proposes a voltage error suppression strategy using five-segment modulation. The strategy begins with the introduction of a control region boundary prediction algorithm. It is designed to predict the ideal voltage output waveform based on discrete sampling signals. Considering that the five-segment switching pattern can reduce current ripple induced by voltage harmonics, this paper presents a combination of the switching pattern with the predicted voltage output waveform. This approach not only considers the limitations on the number of level outputs in five-segment switching pattern but also ensures the accuracy of the reference voltage from the current controller. By predicting the ideal voltage waveform in advance, the proposed strategy can effectively eliminate the time-lag problem in the conventional modulation. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposal in enhancing torque output capability under high-speed conditions is demonstrated through experiments on a 6kW 12/8 SRM experimental platform.

articleTitle: Identification of Mutual Inductance and Load in WPT System Based on Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In the field of magnetically coupled resonant wireless power transmission (MCR-WPT), the dual-parameter identification of mutual inductance and load parameters plays an important role in the development of effective wireless charging solutions for a range of technical devices. The extant parameter identification methods are beset with shortcomings, including slowness, low precision, parameter coupling, and a complex derivation process. This paper puts forth a mutual inductance and load dual-parameter identification method based on neural networks for series-series compensated wireless power transfer (SS WPT) system. By leveraging the non-linear characterisation capabilities of neural networks and integrating the principles of dual-parameter identification, a model for identifying the parameters of a magnetically coupled resonant wireless power transmission system can be constructed. This approach enables the identification process to be completed rapidly and with high precision.

articleTitle: A rapidly calibratable mechanical model of pouch lithium-ion batteries for fast charging conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The stack pressure in lithium-ion battery system shows significant effect on the life span of batteries and stability of whole structure. A precise mechanic model which can predict the stress or strain evolution of the battery during operation is becoming more interested in multi-physics sensors estimation, control, and warning by battery management systems, especially in fast charging conditions. However, the construction and calibration of mechanical models is currently not as efficient and accurate as electrical ones. This paper proposes a rapidly calibratable mechanical model of pouch lithium-ion batteries, aiming at coping with a wide range of rate and temperature variations in fast charging scenarios. Free-swelling property of the battery at different charging rates are pre-discussed, and thermal expansion is decoupled at the same time. An in-process compression modulus’ rapid identification method is then executed in multiple temperatures and preloading, providing comprehensive state of charge (SOC)-thermal-stress three-factor mechanical parameters. A Commercial LiNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pouch battery is chosen for modeling and validation. A typical multi-stage charging strategy is finally used to verify the accuracy of the proposed model. The results show that the proposed mechanical model has sufficient accuracy as well as strong adaptability in fast charging scenarios.

articleTitle: State of Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on Improved Support Vector Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: To solve the problems with imprecise aging feature extraction and time-consuming parameter optimization in current data-driven lithium-ion battery state of health (SOH) estimation algorithms, an improved support vector regression (SVR) algorithm is proposed for accurate SOH prediction. First, the aging data of lithium-ion batteries are preprocessed using incremental capacity curves to extract key factors representing the battery’s aging state, which are then validated through grey relation analysis (GRA). Subsequently, the enhanced whale optimization algorithm (EWOA) is employed to optimize the kernel function parameters of the SVR algorithm. This enables the accurate estimation of the battery’s SOH based on the optimized SVR model. Finally, the model’s accuracy is validated by comparing it with traditional support vector machines (SVM), gaussian process regression (GPR), and extreme learning machine (ELM). The results indicate that the optimized SVR model developed in this study is capable of accurately estimating the SOH of the battery, with a maximum estimation error of less than 3%.

articleTitle: The common-mode voltage suppression method for PMSM based on current predictive control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The traditional common-mode voltage (CMV) suppression method, based on current predictive control model, exhibits a significant issue with large current harmonics. This paper proposes a common-mode voltage suppression method based on model predictive control, which can reduce the common-mode voltage and current harmonics of the motor under various working conditions. Firstly, the structure of the two-level voltage source inverters (2L-VSIs) is analyzed, and the reasons for the generation of common-mode voltage are obtained. Secondly, the implementation principle of the virtual vector method is given and a non-zero vector modulation method based on current predictive control is proposed. The calculation method of the action time corresponding to each vector is also given. Then, in order to reduce the current prediction error caused by model parameter mismatch, a Romberg observer with feedforward compensation function is added to the proposed control system. The current prediction performance of the model is further improved. Finally, simulation and experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively attenuate the common-mode voltage and significantly reduce the current harmonics.

articleTitle: A Novel Battery Balancing Topology Coupled with Battery Reconfiguration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The inconsistency between series-connected batteries is a key factor affecting the high performance and lifespan of lithium-ion battery packs. Therefore, a battery balancing system is needed to achieve effective energy balance. Traditional battery balancing is mainly divided into three methods: P2C (Pack to Cell), C2P (Cell to Pack), and C2C (Cell to Cell). The C2C structure is complex and hard to control, while the other two have the issue of repeated balancing. To address this issue, this paper proposes a battery balancing system coupled with battery reconfiguration based on flyback transformation. In order to enhance the controllability of the battery balancing system, the topology of the balancing system adopts the C2P/P2C method, and the balancing direction can be switched according to the current situation during the balancing process. To avoid the problem of repeated balancing, each battery is connected in parallel with a bypass circuit based on battery reconfiguration. Through a series of simulation, it can be concluded that this battery balancing system has good robustness, solves the problem of repeated balancing, and the balancing efficiency has improved.

articleTitle: Optimization and Characterisation of Flat-wire Permanent Magnet Motors for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) are favoured in the field of electric vehicles because of their advantages such as high power density and high efficiency. In this paper, a flat wire winding is applied to a PMSM, and a flat-wire PMSM is designed to improve the slot fullness and heat dissipation performance, and further enhance the motor performance. According to the design index of the motor, the motor structure and preliminary electromagnetic parameters are determined. A finite element model of the motor is established to analyse the influence of the stator and rotor structural parameters on the torque and torque ripple of the motor, and the rotor auxiliary slot is used to reduce the torque ripple. The electromagnetic characteristics of the motor are studied and analysed, and the efficiency Map is drawn to obtain the highest efficiency of 96.55%, and the percentage of the efficient operation area with an efficiency greater than 85% is 91.5%. The results show that the motor meets the design indexes and the needs of electric vehicle drive motors, and provides a basis for the design of this type of motor.

articleTitle: Sensorless control strategy for SPMSM with improved full-order sliding mode observer and novel converged switching strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In pursuit of improving both the estimation accuracy and dynamic performance of sensorless control technology of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM), this article proposes the higher-order terminal sliding mode control on the basis of the full-order state equation. Through rigorous theoretical derivation, this study substantiates the stability and rapid convergence of the proposed scheme. Meanwhile, this research addresses the demands of a wide speed range by introducing a novel adaptive switching strategy. This strategy dynamically modulates the amplitude of the square-wave injected signal in response to variations in motor speed. This approach mitigates the impact of the injected signal amplitude on the sliding mode observer within the transition zone and it facilitates smooth transitions between the two sensorless control algorithms. Finally, the overall control scheme is validated through experimental results, demonstrating the capability to achieve wide speed range acceleration and deceleration from 0 to 1000 r/min, and seamless transitions between the two control strategies.

articleTitle: Mechanical finite element analysis and electromagnetic compatibility optimization of nickel-plated carbon fiber composite high-frequency box shell material
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The high-frequency box shell simulation calculation is one of the main means to evaluate the qualification of high-frequency box shell structure. The external conditions can affect the strength and stability of the high-frequency box shell and can indirectly affect the accuracy of the use of the high-frequency box shell, which can lead to the deformation and damage of the structure. With the help of computational mechanics software, this paper provides effective data support for the design of radar high-frequency box shells by using several modeling methods under selected loads to calculate the high-frequency box shells. In addition to the role of mechanical protection, the high-frequency box of electronic equipment needs to be used to solve the important function of shielding electromagnetic interference. The electromagnetic compatibility of the chassis is one of the important means to solve the electromagnetic compatibility problem of electronic equipment.

articleTitle: A novel lithium-ion battery state of charge estimation method based on the fusion of neural network and equivalent circuit models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Accurate State of Charge (SOC) estimation plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety and efficiency of lithium-ion batteries. The existing data-driven SOC estimation methods usually use the directly measured feature information to estimate SOC, resulting in a large calculation error. This paper presents a SOC estimation method which combines the equivalent circuit model (ECM) with the gated cycle unit (GRU) neural network. Firstly, the terminal voltage of the battery is obtained independently through a second-order resistance-capacitance model and GRU. Then, the error weight method is introduced to process the voltage data obtained by ECM and GRU, which help to reduce the influence of terminal voltage error on the final SOC estimation result. To improve the robustness of the system, the difference between the processed terminal voltage and the actual output voltage is synchronously imported into the GRU as an additional feature to increase the input dimension of the model data. Lastly, the proposed SOC estimation method is evaluated under the dynamic current condition. Compared with the single data-driven method, the root-mean-square error of the proposed SOC estimation method is reduced by 1%. The results show that the proposed method has better accuracy.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation of the D/Q Axis Inductance of a Hybrid Excitation Generator with Interlaced Magnetic Poles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The magnetic circuit structure of the interleaved pole hybrid excitation generator is complex, and the use of three-dimensional finite element method to calculate the inductance of this type of generator has the drawbacks of high computational complexity and long time consumption. This article combines the equivalent current sheet and subdomain method to propose an inductance analytical model for hybrid excitation generators that can consider different pole slot combinations and different winding phases, achieving rapid calculation of the D/Q axis composite flux and inductance of this type of generator. During the modeling process, based on the characteristics of the generator’s magnetic circuit, its complex three-dimensional structure can be equivalent to the axial superposition of two-dimensional auxiliary excitation, permanent magnet, and DC excitation regions. By establishing sub domain models for different regions, the armature reaction inductance can be calculated. The calculation results can be stacked to obtain the original generator's D/Q axis inductance. Finally, an experimental verification was conducted on a three-phase interleaved pole hybrid excitation generator, and the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed analytical model were verified by comparing the analytical meter, finite element analysis, and experimental results. Compared to the finite element method, the required model can reduce the calculation time by more than 97% while ensuring calculation accuracy, effectively improving the efficiency of generator inductance calculation, which provides convenience for the initial design and optimization of related types of generators.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Cell Balancing Methods for High Capacity Electric Vehicle Lithium-ion Battery Packs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: There are generally two types of voltage-based balancing for lithium batteries: top and bottom balancing. Top balancing is practical for small electric vehicles as charging overnight fills up and balances the batteries. Larger and heavier electric vehicles, on the other hand, do not enjoy such convenience. They need proper infrastructure just to charge quickly without problems with the local electric grid. Factoring balancing delay with other considerations could mean bottom balancing might be more appropriate. This paper analyzes the balancing time as well as other considerations when choosing whether to utilize top or bottom balancing for high-capacity battery systems in electric vehicles.

articleTitle: A sliding virtual primary adaptive parameter identification method for linear induction motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The secondary thermal effect of the ultra-high-speed linear induction motor significantly impacts thrust output and speed enhancement. The segmentation structure of the linear motor causes dynamic changes in primary voltage and current with the rapid moving of secondary. This paper proposes a sliding virtual primary adaptive parameter identification method, it weights and equates the primary voltage and magnetic flux of the effective parts of each primary segment according to the coverage ratio. The reference and adjustable model of the proposed method are not affected by the segmented structure, it can improve the accuracy of identification of the secondary resistance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed virtual primary identification method can accurately identify the secondary resistance

articleTitle: A Low-Temperature Self-Heating Method with Temperature Consistency Control Capability Based on Reconfigurable Battery System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In the process of low temperature heating, the temperature rise of the batteries is significantly different, which is mainly because of the inconsistency of the internal resistance of the battery and the inconsistency of the thermal resistance between the battery and the external environment. Battery temperature inconsistency not only leads to nonuniform aging, but also causes the battery energy to be excessively consumed. In order to eliminate the inconsistent temperature rise of the battery in the process of low temperature heating, this paper proposes a low temperature self-heating method with local temperature control capability based on reconfigurable battery system. This innovative method can uniformly raise the temperature of the battery under extreme conditions, and significantly reduce energy consumption and heating time. Firstly, the reconfigurable battery system is designed and the modular reconfiguration topology is proposed. Secondly, the local temperature control heating strategy is designed and analyzed. Finally, the proposed heating method is verified.

articleTitle: Research on the Compatibility of European Standard Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Against the backdrop of growing global focus on the environment and sustainable transportation, the electric vehicle (EV) market is experiencing rapid growth. China's new energy automotive industry has made leapfrog progress, and the industry ecosystem is becoming increasingly mature. Numerous domestic car manufacturers have begun to actively plan and explore the international market, further expanding their global influence. The popularization of electric vehicles still faces many challenges. Among them, charging issues are particularly prominent and are one of the most important concerns for EV users. Therefore, optimizing the charging experience has become a core direction for technological innovation in the automotive industry. This article focuses on the compatibility of European standard (Euro standard) charging for electric vehicles and provides an in-depth analysis and discussion of the factors affecting the success rate of charging.

articleTitle: A Bi-subspace Model Predictive Controller Based on Incremental Model for the Dual Three-phase PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The presence of current harmonics stemming from the permanent magnet (PM) flux linkage harmonics poses a significant challenge in dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor drives. In this paper, we propose an incremental model based on a bi-subspace virtual vector predictive current controller. Compared to the conventional model-based methods, the incremental model does not rely on prior knowledge of the PM flux linkage parameter, which can vary according to the operating conditions of the drive. Moreover, by incorporating a higher number of data steps in the prediction, the proposed incremental model ensures more accurate tracking of the reference currents and minimizes current harmonics induced by uncertainties in the PM flux linkage. Based on simulation results, this digest provides a comparison between the conventional and the incremental model-based bi-subspace virtual vector predictive current control methods.

articleTitle: Efficiency Optimization of IPT System Based on Coils with Nanocrystalline Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In long-distance inductive power transfer (IPT) applications, the coils are usually with magnetic cores to enhance magnetic field coupling. In this paper, ultra-thin nanocrystalline cores are used as the magnetic cores of IPT system and the coil design method is given. By finite element analysis (FEA) simulation, the feasibility of simplifying the structure of nanocrystalline cores is analyzed, and the reliability of the whole system embedded in 110kV insulator has been demonstrated. In addition, this paper puts forward a method to optimize IPT system efficiency for a given load, and verifies the effectiveness of this method through simulation and experiment. A 1.5m five-coil system with nanocrystalline cores is constructed and the experimental results show that the efficiency can be improved significantly, especially in the case of large load resistance.

articleTitle: Effect of Test Voltage Waveforms on Partial Discharge Inception Voltage Considering Different Environmental Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Electrical machines (EMs) used in transportation applications are subjected to high voltage stress due to the elevated DC link voltage and fast rise time of switching devices. These design choices promote partial discharge (PD) activity in winding insulation, which in turn jeopardizes EM safe operations. PD tests can be conducted using either sinusoidal or impulse voltage waveforms; however, variations in test results may arise from different test voltage types, particularly when considering the harsh ambient conditions encountered by transportation EMs. Therefore, it is essential to assess this discrepancy and its dependence on ambient conditions. In this study, the partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) is measured under four distinct ambient conditions: 100°C at 1000 mbar; 100°C at 400 mbar; 180°C at 1000 mbar; and 180°C at 400 mbar. The mismatches between test results are emphasized and a stress voltage waveform enhancement factor is proposed. Based on this factor, the PD risk could be simply evaluated by referring to the PD test results obtained by applying a sinusoidal voltage as a stress waveform.

articleTitle: Two-stage Hydrogen Converter Based on 48-pulse Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: To enhance the input performance of conventional two-stage hydrogen converters and reduce input current harmonics, this paper proposes a two-stage hydrogen converter with a 48-pulse rectifier as the front-end circuit. The proposed 48-pulse rectifier consists of a conventional 24-pulse rectifier combined with a tapped interphase reactor (T-IPR). The diodes on the T-IPR are alternately switched based on the polarity of the input voltage, thereby enhancing the output states of the rectifier bridge. This increases the rectifier’s pulse count from 24 to 48, reducing the hydrogen converter's input current harmonics to below 5% and achieving an approximately sinusoidal input current. The proposed hydrogen rectifier front-end offers excellent harmonic suppression, a simple structure, low cost, and high reliability, indicating promising application prospects. A simulation model of the two-stage hydrogen converter was developed using simulation software, validating the harmonic suppression effectiveness of the proposed 48-pulse rectifier front-end.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of High-speed Permanent Magnet Starter Generators with Toroidal Windings and Lap Windings for Aviation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Since the rotor flux is fixed and cannot be controlled or disengaged when a short circuit (SC) is initiated, high-speed permanent magnet starter generator (HSPMSG) exhibits a significant interturn short-circuit (ITSC) or end short-SC current, which can lead to overheating and pose risks to the reliability and safety of the generating system. This paper comprehensively analyzes and compares the electromagnetic characteristics of toroidal-winding and lap-winding HSPMSGs under normal operation, winding end SC fault, and ITSC fault. The toroidal-winding HSPMSG was found having comparable electromagnetic performance with lap-winding HSPMSG under normal operation, but has stronger ability to suppress the SC current, especially for the ITSC fault. Finally, a toroidal-winding HSPMSG prototype was fabricated and the theorical analysis was verified.

articleTitle: Performances comparison of PMSM and SRM for EV aiming for maximum speed of 50,000 min-1
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this research, two motor types, PMSM and SRM, which targeted the output power of 85 kW and the maximum speed of 52,000 min<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, are designed for EV traction motors. The mechanical and electrical properties are evaluated and compared by Finite Element Analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: Electromagnetic and Thermal Coupling and Cooling Optimization of Traction Motors in Electric Powertrains
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, a comprehensive analysis coupling the electromagnetic and thermal behavior of traction motors in electric powertrains, and an optimization of the motor cooling system is presented. In heat generation of the traction motor, electromagnetic losses including DC winding losses, AC winding losses, and core losses are discussed. The skin effect due to the eddy current in the winding and the proximity effect in AC winding fosses are added based on correction factors of the DC winding fosses. Modified Steinmetz equations are used to calculate the core fosses. In the heat dissipation part, empirical formulations of the natural and forced convection heat transfer which match the geometrical shapes of electric motors are discussed. Moreover, to increase the accuracy further with a minimal cost of computational time, a one-dimensional and three-dimensional synergetic approach is proposed and implemented in the model. As a study case, four types of forced cooling systems of a traction motor are designed and modeled with the proposed method. The results validate the capability of this workflow and provide a solid reference for the optimization of the thermal design of the traction motors in electric powertrains.

articleTitle: Open-Loop Sweep Based Multi-Frequency Motor Parameters Correction Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The conventional controller tuning technique depends on plant parameters, hence the precision of plant parameter identification significantly impacts the stability margin and dynamic capability of the system. In recent years, numerous parameter identification approaches have been suggested for both online and offline applications combined with modern control theory or optimal control theory. Nevertheless, as a result of the system's non-linearity and unmodeled dynamics, certain identification procedures yield poor outcomes, resulting in a reduction in stability margin and degradation of the system's dynamic responsiveness. This article propose a parameter correction approach based on open-loop sweep that operates at many frequencies, The technique utilises the amplitude- and phase-frequency properties of open-loop transfer function to accurately identity delay constant in the high-frequency band and correct mismatch parameters in the middle- and low-frequency band. The simulation results demonstrate that this technique effectively corrects the mismatched motor parameters and enables the system to attain a suitable stability margin and dynamic capability.

articleTitle: Analytical Investigation of the Electromagnetic Performance of a Novel M-Core Modular Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A novel permanent magnet (PM) machine with an M-core stator modular structure is proposed in this article. Firstly, the structure and operation principle of the stator modular motor are illustrated. Then, the electromagnetic performance of the proposed motor is investigated by an analytical model and finite element analysis (FEA), including no-load air-gap flux density, flux linkage, back electromotive force (EMF), and electromagnetic torque. Finally, the electromagnetic performance of the proposed motor is compared with that of motors with other stator modular structures, and the analytical model is verified by means of FEA. The results show that the proposed motor can achieve similar torque output with less iron core usage, improve the power density of the motor, and have stronger heat dissipation potential, making it very suitable for use in aircraft applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of Effective Dual Optimization Torque Control for Electronic Power Steering System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The electronic power steering system requires the performance of rapid and robust. This paper first proposes a control method where a transition angle variable is designed to avoid shock response once angle sudden changes, using Laplace transform to get the approximate angular speed signal and transition angle both merged to determine the target torque of control loop, In addition, the disturbance observer is designed to identify unknown noise which is used to compensate in the control loop to suppress ripple of torque. Both simulation model of control scheme and experiments will be performed to verify the feasibility.

articleTitle: Investigation of Data Parameters for Online Calculation of EIS based on Power Batteries with Different Capacities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) is a critical parameter for assessing battery performance. Utilizing multi-frequency signals, such as step signals, enables the calculation of EIS, which holds significant potential for practical applications. This study employs step signals in conjunction with the S-transform algorithm to derive the EIS of batteries. However, the accuracy of the calculated EIS is influenced by the quality and parameters of the input signals. This article investigates the effects of sampling frequency, signal duration, and current amplitude on the results obtained from current step signals, incorporating both experimental and simulation approaches. Three types of batteries with different capacities are considered. The findings provide valuable insights for enhancing the application of impedance spectra in future calculations.

articleTitle: A Distributed Virtual Inertia Enhancement Control of an Islanded DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The recent advancement in DC microgrid is attributable to the emerging technologies developed on distributed renewables power generation and storage. Power electronic converters act as an interface in integrating large scale renewable energy sources and energy storage systems to DC microgrid, enabling in either utility grid connected mode or in islanded mode. However, the inertia of an islanded DC microgrid is lower compared to a utility grid connected DC microgrid, mainly due to the full dependency on renewable energy sources for power generation, the absence of inertia supported by synchronous generators, and the low inertia of power electronic converters. Consequently, DC bus voltage fluctuation is severe during transient power variations caused by the intermittent renewable energy sources and dynamic loading. In this work, a new power management methodology integrating three control modes, based on distributed virtual inertia enhancement control method, is proposed for maintaining the stability of DC bus voltage of an islanded DC microgrid. The proposed idea helps in providing instant inertia support to the system through distributed virtual DC-link capacitors, i.e., without implementing any physical components, which is a cost-free and space saving approach. The generated power, load power requirement, and battery state-of-charge information of the energy storage system are utilized to implement different control modes. A MATLAB simulation model of the system has been developed for preliminary verification. It is observed that the DC bus voltage fluctuation could be dramatically reduced to ≤ 0.7% of nominal value with the proposed method.

Author Keywords: Islanded DC micro grid and virtual inertia control

articleTitle: A Speed Loop Control Strategy for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Based on Reduced-Dimensional EMPC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: EMPC, with its fast dynamic response and strong robustness, is highly suitable for the outer loop control of servo systems. However, due to the lengthy execution time and high memory consumption of the algorithm, EMPC is only suitable for solving small-scale problems. Additionally, its dependency on parameters limits its application under complex operating conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a reduced-dimensional EMPC control strategy for the speed loop of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM). By reconstructing the speed loop model, the algorithm’s dimensionality is reduced to only 2, significantly decreasing the algorithm’s complexity. The algorithm’s reliance on parameters is significantly decreased by using an Extended State Observer (ESO) to observe speed disturbances. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the improved algorithm possesses strong disturbance rejection capability and robustness, while maintaining low algorithmic complexity.

articleTitle: A two-stage day-ahead optimization method for berth allocation and energy system in seaport under time-of-use electricity prices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Port is an important node of maritime transportation network. In recent years, there has been heightened attention to environmental issues, causing a crucial challenge for port operators to reduce energy consumption and pollution. Ships can generate much pollution when utilizing auxiliary engines at berth and onshore power is an important means to solve ship emissions. However, the utilization of onshore power is affected by electricity price. With the development of renewable energy, the integrated energy system in port can reduce purchasing electricity from the utility and therefore promote onshore power usage. Therefore, we present a two-stage day-ahead scheduling method aiming to harmonize the optimization of berth allocation problem (BAP) and energy system scheduling problem(ESSP). In the first stage, our proposed model aims at minimizing delay time of each ship and maximizing the utilization of onshore power. In the second stage, our model optimizes the operation of energy system to minimize the energy consumption cost and the start-up cost of different energy facilities. In the above model, we consider the influence of time-of-use electricity prices on both two stages. Experimental results show that the proposed model effectively promotes the utilization of shore power facilities and reduces reliance on fossil fuels.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of Onboard Electrical Grids in Pure Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Researchers conducted a study on the stability of on-board electrical networks in response to challenges such as limited power capacity, diverse types of inverters, and complex operating conditions in electric power systems for new energy vehicles. This paper focuses on small-signal modeling of the electrical system in pure electric vehicles, deriving the output impedance of each power source and the input impedance of the load motor. Based on impedance analysis, this paper proposes impedance design rules for vehicle electrical systems. Using Bode plots, it explores the impact of key parameters on system stability. Finally, simulations effectively validated the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed analysis method. The research findings indication: Super capacitors can mitigate the voltage transients on the busbar caused by vehicle startup and load changes, the inductance value of the DC/DC converter's induction coil also affects the stability of the busbar voltage, what’s more, variations in the torque and speed of the drive motor also influence busbar voltage stability. For the pure electric vehicle studied in this paper, the induction coil value of the DC/DC converter should range from 0.001H to 0.016H. The torque variation of the motor should not exceed 220 N·m and the speed variation should not exceed 2000 rpm.

articleTitle: Research on Temperature Field of Low Speed High Torque Integrated Motor Based on Improved Equivalent Thermal Network Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced equivalent thermal network model to simultaneously calculate the temperature rise of both the motor and the inverter when addressing the temperature field of a low-speed, high-torque integrated permanent magnet motor (LSHTIPMM) with drive control devices at the end, given the substantial computational demands of the three-dimensional finite element method(3D-FEM). The model assesses the steady-state temperature rise at critical nodes within the motor and switching devices. A comparison between the model’s results and those obtained through 3D-FEM confirms the model’s accuracy and efficiency. The improved thermal network method shows an error margin of only 0.73% - 2.73% compared to 3D-FEM, satisfying accuracy demands, while requiring only 1% of the finite element method’s computation time. This offers superior guidance for the initial thermal structure design and component selection in integrated motors, enabling more compact integration through thermal design.

articleTitle: Performance Analyses of a High-Frequency Transformers With Different Magnetic Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Taking advantages of the high power density and high efficiency, High Frequency Transformers (HFT) have been widely applied in the electrified transportation. However, the low saturation flux density and large core loss has limited the increase of the power. In the paper, the core loss calculation method of HFT operated under high frequency non-sinusoidal excitation are presented. Then the flux density and efficiency of HFT with double E-type and C-type core structures are compared. The finite element method was taken to analyze the performances of HFT with different core materials and different operation current waveforms. The relations of the efficiency with the power, core clearance, and operation frequency are also studied. Then the experimental results are carried out on the prototype of 60 kW HFT to verify the accuracy of the calculation results.

articleTitle: Error Iterative Control Strategy for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Servo System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: With the development of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) servo control system, the requirements for fast response control are increasing, in addition to the requirements for low overshoot.
