However, the inherent power cross-coupling among different ports poses difficulties and challenges for controller design. The conventional proportional-integral (PI) control may lead to steady-state oscillations and slow dynamic response. To mitigate these issues, this paper proposes a finite control set-model predictive control (FCS-MPC) method that eliminates the need for complex decoupling matrix design and can achieve good dynamic response. This strategy establishes a finite control set to directly predict the phase shift ratio, thereby achieving control of voltage and power distribution.

articleTitle: Voltage-Behind-Reactance Model of Dual-Three PMSM Considering Fault Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In the simulation of winding faults in Dual-Three Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (DTPMSM), the traditional model only applies to the healthy operating state and cannot accurately reflect the operation condition of the DTPMSM in winding fault conditions, so it is necessary to establish a model of DTPMSM that can be suitable for both healthy and faulty conditions. To solve this problem, a Voltage-Behind-Reactance (VBR) model of DTPMSM considering fault simulation is built in this paper, which realizes a direct connection between the DTPMSM and the power electronic circuits and applies to different operating conditions including open-circuit and short-circuit fault. The VBR model of the DTPMSM is verified through comparison with FEA simulations and is of great significance for the in-depth investigation of the simulation and analysis of the fault-tolerant control of DTPMSM.

articleTitle: Rapid non-destructive testing method for moisture content of insulating paper based on terahertz technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: As an electrical insulating material, oil paper is widely used in electric motors and their related equipments. The moisture content of insulating paper directly affects its insulating ability, and at the same time, it will reduce the mechanical strength and abrasion resistance of insulating paper. In order to solve the deficiencies of the traditional testing methods for insulating paper moisture, which are lossy and cumbersome, this paper realizes the non-destructive testing of insulating paper moisture by using the terahertz technology. Firstly, the relationship between the number distribution of cellulose-water hydrogen bonds and water-water hydrogen bonds and water content was analyzed using Materials Studio software, after which gradient moisture content insulating paper samples were prepared and tested using the built terahertz platform. The theoretical analysis and experimental results show that the relaxation resonance amplitude Aosc can indirectly reflect the number and bond energy of cellulose-water-hydrogen bond and water-water-hydrogen bond, characterize the moisture state and polarization behavior of the oil paper, and have a linear relationship with the water content of insulating paper (R2>0.95), which can be combined with the results of terahertz complex dielectric spectroscopy to invert the insulating paper moisture, and realize the rapid and nondestructive assessment of moisture.

Author Keywords: Terahertz technology Insulation paper Moisture content detection Non-destructive testing

articleTitle: Parameter Identification of Lithium Battery DC/DC Converters Based on Hybrid Systems Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: To address the limitations of traditional mathematical modeling, which fails to fully account for the switching between charging and discharging states of lithium batteries and their interaction with the operating modes of DC/DC converters, a parameter identification method for the control of lithium batteries and DC/DC converters based on hybrid systems theory is proposed. This method aims to suppress output voltage fluctuations under different load conditions. First, a mechanistic mathematical model is established using hybrid systems theory, encompassing the switching states of the lithium battery’s charging and discharging processes as well as the conduction state of the switch. Next, actual experimental data is collected, and the model parameters are identified using the recursive least squares method, clarifying the internal and parasitic parameters. Finally, a corresponding simulation model is built to compare the errors between the experimental and simulation results. The results indicate that the proposed method can effectively simulate the state transitions of the battery and DC/DC converter under different operating modes.

articleTitle: Impact of typical degradation conditions on the output behavior of optimal algorithms for fuel cell hybrid electric vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: As the diversity of energy systems increases, optimizing energy management to maximize the advantages of each system has become a critical issue, especially fuel cell systems, which often need to be integrated with other energy systems. This paper takes fuel cell and battery hybrid vehicles as the research object and studies the impact of four typical degradation working conditions on the optimal energy management strategy by incorporating weighting coefficients into the objective function. Research revealed that the four degradation conditions, in descending order of importance, are: load change, start-stop cycle, high power condition, and idle condition. This research shows that although each degradation cost in the objective function will only occur under the corresponding working condition, they have an interactive effect on the power distribution behavior in multi-energy systems. For example, the presence of load change degradation costs inhibits the occurrence of the other three decay conditions. Surprisingly, the presence of start-stop degradation costs reduces the load change behavior of the fuel cell.

articleTitle: Performances comparison of Reluctance Machines Energized Bipolar and Unipolar Sinusoidal Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, SRM, DC-VRM, and VRM with same pole-slot combinations of 8 poles/12 slots and 10 poles/12 slots are designed, the mechanism of generating torque in the energization by the sinusoidal current with and without DC offset is analyzed by Finite Element Analysis (FEA). Through these analyses, the structure that satisfies high torque and the excitation methods suitable for each speed range in reluctance motors with applying sinusoidal current will be clarified.

articleTitle: Based on the variation of battery cycle attenuation under electrothermal coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: With the economic and social development, the demand for energy is increasing globally, and the environmental problems are becoming more serious, and the massive use of fossil energy such as oil can cause greater environmental pollution problems, in order to reduce environmental pollution and the greenhouse effect, the development of electric vehicles and power batteries are getting more and more attention from the society. Based on the above background, in order to improve the economic and social benefits of electric vehicles, researchers have conducted a large number of related studies on the performance of power batteries. This paper carries out a simulation and analysis study on the performance change of lithium battery under typical working conditions under thermoelectric multi-coupling factors. In this paper, three-dimensional modeling is carried out based on the working characteristics of lithium batteries, which electrochemical model will be used P2D (pseudo two dimensional, P2D) model theory. The main research content of this paper and the results to be obtained are as follows: the use of COMSOL Multiphysics software platform for lithium-ion batteries to establish a three-dimensional electrochemical thermal coupling model; on this basis, through the relevant experimental data, to verify the authenticity and feasibility of the simulation model; the use of the simulation model for the simulation and analysis of the battery performance degradation, to obtain the multi-factorial coupling of heat, electricity, the performance of lithium battery degradation data and patterns. The simulation model is used to simulate and analyze the battery performance degradation to obtain the performance degradation data and law of lithium battery under multi-factor coupling of heat and electricity. Based on the above background, in order to improve the economic and social benefits of electric vehicles, researchers have conducted a large number of related studies on the performance of power batteries. This paper focuses on the influence of different charging and discharging rates on battery performance under normal temperature conditions. It is found that the battery decay rate is the lowest at 0.2C charging rate, and the battery decay rate is the highest at 2C charging rate, which significantly accelerates the battery decay. The charging ratio of 1C is a more optimized choice.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Evaluation Strategy of Charging Station Based on Combination Weighting Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the current evaluation index of charging station is not comprehensive enough and the evaluation method is not perfect enough, the evaluation strategy of charging station is established. Firstly, a double-layer evaluation index system of charging station is established from three dimensions of scale, economy and service. Then, the weights of the three dimensions of the second layer are obtained by the subjective Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), and then the weights of the 12 indicators of the third layer are obtained by the combination weighting method, and the second and third layers are multiplied to obtain the weight of each index. Secondly, the scores of each charging station are calculated by the obtained weights, and the service quality of one charging station is judged macroscopically by fuzzy evaluation. Finally, Importance Performance Analysis (IPA) is used to analyze the indicators that need to be improved in each charging station, which points out the direction for charging stations to improve their own services.

articleTitle: An Extended Droop Control Strategy for More Electric Aircraft Electric Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Power allocation is a major concern in more electric aircraft (MEA). This paper proposes an extended droop control strategy for MEA HVDC composed of permanent synchronous generator (PMSG) and lithium-ion (Li-ion), by implementing virtual resistance droop control to PMSG and virtual capacitor droop control to SC, aiming to achieve dynamic current sharing and stable operation. In order to achieve the control objectives, the system impedance was modeled and the frequency domain characteristics of the system were analyzed. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed control strategy was verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Characterization of Multiplicative Discharge of Lithium Iron Phosphate Batteries at Different Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: As one of the core components of the energy storage system, it is crucial to explore the performance of lithium iron phosphate batteries under different operating conditions. This paper aims to explore the correlation between voltage, capacity and temperature of LiFePO4 batteries by conducting discharge tests at different multiples of the battery in different temperature ranges. To evaluate the specific effects of different temperatures and discharge rates on battery performance. The experimental results indicate that at a conventional discharge rate of 1C, the battery experiences a significant voltage drop within the temperature range of -15°C to 0°C. This voltage drop gradually improves as the temperature rises. Additionally, at low temperatures, the energy efficiency of the battery is typically lower than its capacity efficiency. On the other hand, at high discharge rates, the overall discharge capacity changes only slightly across different temperatures, with variations staying within 5%. Similarly, within the temperature range of 35°C to 55°C, the overall discharge capacity remains relatively consistent, also staying within a 5% difference. It is worth noting that within the 35°C to 55°C temperature range, the overall capacity of a LiFePO4 battery is lower than that of a LiFePO4 battery. In the temperature range of 35°C~55°C, discharge curves at different multiples exhibit similar trends. Specifically, at high multiples within the same temperature range, the overall discharge capacity varies by less than 5%. These findings offer valuable insights for determining the most suitable operating conditions for lithium iron phosphate batteries in real-world scenarios, with significant implications for engineering applications.

articleTitle: The Coupled Analysis of Mechanical and Electromagnetic Interaction for Vehicle Electromagnetic Suspension
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: An electromagnetic suspension is usually described as a device for vibration suppression of vehicle body through electrical machine and its related control device. There are two paths of energy and characteristics to balance with, namely, vibration energy of vehicle wheel and electrical energy of electrical machine, electromagnetic and mechanical characteristics of electrical machine and dynamic characteristics of vehicle suspension. The coupling analysis is manipulated through the derivation between electromagnetic and dynamic control equations which describe the electrical machine and vehicle suspension. A simulation is done through intersection of vehicle suspension and electrical machine. It demonstrates that electromagnetic suspension needs co-control strategy in interdisciplinary studies for better performance of vehicle dynamics and energy saving.

articleTitle: Adaptive Synchronization and Dead-Time Control Method for GaN-Based Full-Bridge Rectifier in MHz Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) technology, particularly in the megahertz (MHz) frequency range, has undergone significant advancements, such as enhanced power transfer efficiency and reduced component size. Gallium nitride high electron mobility transistors (GaN HEMTs) are particularly advantageous for MHz applications due to their superior electrical properties. To further enhance efficiency in WPT systems, synchronous rectification (SR) is employed, which requires precise synchronization control. This paper introduces a novel drain-source voltage sensing (DVS) based body-diode-conduction (BDC) extraction circuit, along with an adaptive synchronization and dead-time control (ASDTC) method. The BDC circuit accurately differentiates between the conduction states of the body diode and the GaN device. And the resulting signal is processed by an FPGA to generate appropriate driving signals for controlling the GaN device’s turn-on and turn-off. This adaptive control system ensures critical Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) turn-on and Zero Current Switching (ZCS) turn-off. The proposed method has been validated through simulation and experimental prototype of a 6.78 MHz GaN-based full-bridge WPT system, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving optimal SR operation with critical-ZVS turn-on and critical -ZCS turn-off.

articleTitle: Internal short circuit diagnosis method based on discharge curve of lithium-ion battery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The internal short circuit (ISC) of lithium-ion battery is one of the common causes of thermal runaway. Therefore, it is necessary to find an effective method to diagnose ISC to avoid thermal runaway and improve battery safety. In this paper, it is found from the battery long-term cycling data set that some batteries are short-circuited during the cycle or after standing that the terminal voltage is 0. In this paper, the ISC diagnosis method is proposed by observing the cycle data of the ISC battery. It is found that due to the polarization of the battery, the area of the discharge curve of the battery at high current rates (1C) and low current rates (1/25C) is different. In this paper, the area of the discharge voltage curve of the battery at high rate and law rate is featured, and ISC diagnosis method is proposed. Specifically, it was found that the decay rate of the area of the discharge curve at law current rates was slower than that at high current rates during battery cycle. The decay rate of the area of ISC cells discharge curve at law current rates is faster than that at high current rates during battery cycle. ISC diagnosis method is proposed based on the results. In the process of battery cycling, if the fitting curve of the area of the discharge curve at high current rates and low current rates has a tendency of "crossing", it can be judged that the battery has occurred ISC.

articleTitle: Effects of Prolonged Storage on the Thermal Stability of NCM/Graphite Lithium-ion Battery: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The safety of lithium-ion batteries throughout their life is intricately related to the aging pathways, including calendar aging and cycle aging under various conditions such as different state of charges, temperatures, resting time, and current rates. When stored for extended periods, Li-ion batteries can undergo side reactions like the gradual thickening of the negative electrode's SEI film. This can result in a reduction of available lithium ions, impacting the battery's capacity and safety. To investigate this issue, a three-year shelf aging experiment was conducted on two pouch-type NCM/Graphite batteries, and the electrochemical and thermal stability were compared between fresh and aged ones. The results suggest a notable enhancement in safety for both batteries following extended storage. This improvement was evidenced by higher self-heating temperatures, longer reaction times, reduced heat release rates during thermal runaway, and an increased activation energy required for reactions. Additionally, differences were observed in the capacity degradation rates and safety profiles of the two ternary system batteries. Batteries that experienced more capacity degradation exhibited more significant enhancements in thermal stability. Therefore, this study offers valuable insights into the correlation between aging processes and the safety of batteries.

articleTitle: A Multi-Pulse Rectifier with a Passive Pulse-Tripling Circuit for Ship Electric Propulsion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: To effectively suppress harmonics generated by the ship electric propulsion system, this paper proposes a multi-pulse rectifier with a passive pulse-tripling circuit for ship electric propulsion. The proposed 36-pulse rectifier consists of a conventional 12-pulse rectifier and a passive pulse-tripling circuit. Firstly, the topology of the proposed multi-pulse rectifier is introduced, and the operational modes of the passive pulse-tripling circuit are analyzed in detail. Depending on the magnitude and polarity of the balanced reactor input voltage, the circuit can operate in four different states, thereby increasing the output states of the rectifier bridge. Based on this, the optimal turns ratio of the balanced reactor is derived to minimize the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of the input current. The analysis results show that with the optimal turns ratio of the balanced reactor, the pulse-tripling effect can be achieved, upgrading the 12-pulse rectifier to a 36-pulse rectifier, reducing the THD of the input current to about one-third of the original value, and obtaining an approximately sinusoidal input current, effectively reducing harmonics injected from the ship electric propulsion system into the ship grid. The proposed passive pulse-tripling circuit does not require active components and its capacity is only 3.4% of the output power, demonstrating advantages such as simple circuit structure, high reliability, ease of implementation, and low cost. A simulation model is built to verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the harmonic suppression performance of the proposed ship power propulsion system with passive pulse-tripling.

articleTitle: Multi-Source Data Fusion based EV Charging Behavior Pattern Extraction and Modeling of Coupled Power-Traffic Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) and fast charging stations has created stronger interdependency between urban traffic networks and power networks. Behind the macroscopic power-traffic coupling is the complex microscopic traveling-charging behavior of numerous EV drivers, whose differentiated preferences and bounded rationality calls for more accurate modeling. In this work based on academic-industrial cooperation, a multi-source big data fusion framework is proposed, where EV trajectory, charging station records, trip/parking pattern statistics, traffic condition statistics, and point of interest (POI) maps from EV big data center and charging service companies in Shanghai, China are integrated. Firstly, from the macro-level perspective, vital influencing factors to EV charging are mined. Then, from the micro-level perspective, the bounded rationality of EV drivers is fitted by a discrete choice model, and their differentiated preference is further clustered into several categories. Finally, combining the traffic network dynamics, an augmented stochastic user equilibrium model is proposed for the integrated modeling of coupled power-traffic network flow.

articleTitle: Direct Speed Control of PMSM Based on Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive system, due to the influence of the conventional cascade controller structure, the speed loop control has the problem of slow response speed and speed overshoot. A direct speed control method based on linear active disturbance rejection controller (DSC-ADRC) is proposed to improve the speed control bandwidth and enhance system robustness. Moreover, the introduction of DSC-ADRC design method not only reduces the control parameters, but also gives the physical meaning of each parameter, which has a remarkable effect on reducing the complexity of parameter tuning. The validity and availability of the proposed method are proved through simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Improved SVPWM Strategy and Its Hybrid Technique to Reduce PWM Sideband Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, the sideband harmonic suppression and PWM noise reduction of PMSM are studied. Random zero vector duration SVPWM (RZVD-SVPWM) is proposed. RZVD-SVPWM has an obvious harmonic suppression effect on even times of switching frequency and it is easy to implement. However, its effect on harmonic suppression of twice the switching frequency needs to be strengthened to adapt to scenes with low noise requirements. Hybrid random zero vector duration SVPWM (HRZVD-SVPWM) is proposed to further improve the suppression effect of harmonics with twice the switching frequency. The simulation results show that RZVD-SVPWM and HRZVD-SVPWM have better suppression effect on sideband harmonics than conventional SVPWM. Among them, HRZVD-SVPWM is more complex to implement, but it has better effect on noise reduction.

articleTitle: A TVS Array based Transient Voltage Mitigation Strategy for High Power SSPC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The development of high-voltage DC power supply systems in more electric aircraft (MEA) pushes the development of traditional mechanical contactor-based secondary power distribution systems towards intelligent solid state power distribution systems. As a core component of intelligent power distribution systems, the solid-state power controller (SSPC) has been widely applied in the secondary power distribution systems of MEA. To protect the main power switches from being destroyed by the voltage spike when interrupting high fault current, Transient Voltage Suppressors (TVS) is normally connected in parallel with the main switch to absorb the energy stored in the line parasitic inductance during the protection process. Currently, existing research mainly focus on voltage spike mitigation strategy using a single TVS, since TVSs is not recommended to operate in parallel by the manufactures. However, as the power rating of the SSPC increases, a single TVS is not capable of fully absorb the energy stored in the line inductance, and thus may suffer from overheat failure during turning off. To address this issue, this paper proposes a TVS array based voltage spike mitigation circuit, which significantly increases the energy absorption capability of the voltage mitigation circuit through series and parallel connection of TVSs. Finally, a 270V/180A DC SSPC is designed, and the effectiveness of the proposed voltage mitigation strategy is validated.

articleTitle: Designing and optimizing axial flux motor for electric ships
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid sensitivity analysis and response surface optimization method for the design of an axial flux permanent magnet (AFPM) motor with a yokeless and segmented armature for electric ships’ applications. The initial design parameters are determined using formulas and design experience, and then refined through iterative finite element simulations. Ansys Maxwell is employed for the construction of a finite element model with suitable meshing, with the objective of validating the magnetic circuit design and performance indicators. Taguchi orthogonal experiments are conducted to calculate sensitivity indices, distinguishing between strong- and weak-sensitive parameters. The BBD method is employed for experiments on strong-sensitive parameters, while the NSGA-II algorithm is utilized to identify Pareto optimal solutions. Finite element simulations are conducted to compare motor performance before and after optimization, thereby confirming the effectiveness of multi-objective optimization.

articleTitle: Quasi-resonant Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Current Harmonic Suppression in Vector-Controlled PMSMs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: To suppress the current harmonics of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM), a quasi-resonant active disturbance rejection control (QRADRC) with harmonic extractor method is proposed. The quasi-resonant controller (QRC) is embedded in the control law and operates in parallel with the extended state observer (ESO). The conventional ESO is employed to estimate DC disturbances, while the parallel QRC is utilized to estimate AC disturbances. The three-phase currents are extracted through a harmonic extractor for voltage compensation under αβ coordinate. As a result, the new QRADRC can effectively suppress DC disturbances such as those caused by motor parameter variations, and also greatly improve the suppression of current harmonic AC disturbances with stronger robustness. The effectiveness of QRADRC is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Triple Active Bridge DC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The triple active bridge (TAB) is a promising 3-port DC-DC converter technology which performs bi-directional power transfer with galvanic isolation. Due to intensive interactions between parameter selection and a TAB converter’s performance in efficiency, specific power, reliability, and cost, many design considerations need to be simultaneously weighed to achieve an optimal converter. In this paper, a genetic algorithm based design optimization framework is developed to enhance the performance of a TAB converter with respect to multiple design objectives. Switching devices, thermal management systems, passive components, and the design of a planar multi-winding transformer are accounted for to ensure multidisciplinary performance benefits. Initial optimization results when aiming to attain the highest specific power and efficiency are presented, and the related design trade-offs are discussed.

articleTitle: A Reinforcement Learning Based Operation Optimization of Multi-Energy Island Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: As global carbon emissions and fossil fuel consumption increase, the widely utilization of renewable energy have drawn more attention. Island regions, endowed with abundant renewable resources, present a critical opportunity for low-carbon development. This paper introduces a deep reinforcement learning based optimization framework to improve a multi-energy island microgrid. Furthermore, an innovative approach using a fusion model of Transformer and LSTM to predict wind and solar energy outputs, significantly improving the accuracy of renewable energy forecasts. Case analysis results indicate that with the support of the proposed reinforcement learning method, the economic and operation benefits of multi-energy microgrids on islands are achieved and the operational stability is also enhanced.

articleTitle: Regional Photovoltaic Power Stations Cluster Considering the Spatial-temporal Correlation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: RAs distributed photovoltaic (PV) continues to develop, the accuracy of power prediction for regional clusters of distributed PV power stations directly influences the stable operation of the power system. Accurate distributed PV division is useful for regional distributed PV power prediction. This paper proposes a fuzzy-c means (FCM) clustering method considering spatial and temporal correlation between different distributed PV. Firstly, the astronomical and geographical elements of PV stations are used as primary division indicators, and then the information of PV component parameter of each cluster is used as secondary division indicators. A complete two-level PV power station cluster division method is formed by FCM clustering algorithm. Finally, the effectiveness of the clustering method used in this paper is validated.

articleTitle: Analysis of Vehicle-to-Grid Loads in Coupled Transportation and Power Distribution Network Based on Microscopic Traffic Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The number of electric vehicles is increasing rapidly, and the electric vehicle charging load is exerting a greater impact on the power distribution network. A V2G-compatible program is proposed, constructing a model considering the microscopic behavior of vehicles in the urban transportation network. The proposed program is able to perform a simulation of the coupled transportation and power distribution network. A case of a 37-junction transportation network and the IEEE 33-node distribution network is proposed, and V2G is enabled at a given period of time in this case. The results of the simulation on the proposed case reveal that the proposed program is able to characterize the dynamic changes in traffic flow and charging load and to analyze the impact of V2G on the given case.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Droop Control Method for SOC Balancing in DC Microgrids with Photovoltaic and Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative control method for balancing the state of charge (SOC) in a DC microgrid that integrates a photovoltaic (PV) system and an energy storage system (ESS). The method balances the SOC of the two battery storage units through adaptive sag control, which dynamically adjusts the sag coefficients based on the difference in SOC between the battery storage units. The PV system employs the Incremental Conductance (IncCond) Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) technique to ensure optimal power output. The inner loop of the control system performs current regulation through Model Predictive Control (MPC), while the outer loop manages the bus voltage through sag control. Simulation results show that the system is effective in maintaining SOC balance under different load conditions. The scheme operates at a bus voltage of 400 V and successfully balances the SOC during charge/discharge cycles as the load is dynamically varied from 16 Ω to 8 Ω. In addition, the paper provides several key equations to illustrate the exact operation of the control mechanism.

articleTitle: A Partial Charging Curve-Based Remaining Capacity Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Accurate remaining capacity prediction is of great significance to ensure battery safety and improve state of charge (SOC) estimation. However, current prediction methods neglect user charging habits, leading to difficult feature extraction and inaccurate capacity estimation. This study proposes a partial voltage-based remaining capacity estimation method considering user charging behavior. Firstly, the coverage probability of various SOC charging processes based on real-world driving data is analyzed and the charging duration at equal voltage is extracted as the health feature. Then, the correlation between the health feature and remaining capacity is calculated based on the Pearson correlation coefficient. Subsequently, a joint optimization objective function is established, combining cumulative probability density function and correlation, to determine the optimal voltage range using a particle swarm optimization algorithm. Finally, a temporal convolutional network model is proposed to capture the implicit nonlinear relationship between charging duration within the optimal voltage range and remaining capacity. Across-validation shows that the proposed can track the reference capacity accurately, and the estimation error can be guided within 2.3% of the nominal capacity.

articleTitle: Net Power Enhancement of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell System under Variable Altitude Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In the high-altitude environment, the thin oxygen and low atmospheric pressure diminish the net power of the proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) system. In order to solve this problem, a net power enhancement strategy (NPES) for high altitude is proposed. Based on the close energy interaction between the system and environment, the PEMFC system model for high altitude is established. The oxygen excess ratio (OER) optimization trajectories for variable altitude environments are derived by conducting net power characteristic tests of PEMFC system in various high-altitude environments. Based on this result, a sliding mode control is used to realize the net power enhancement of the PEMFC system. Tests are carried out on the constructed RT-LAB semi-physical platform for validation, and the results show that the NPES proposed in this paper can improve the net power of the PEMFC system under variable altitude conditions.

articleTitle: A Novel Axial-Flux Permanent Magnet Vernier Machine With H-Core Stator Modules and Toroidal Windings for Electric Aircraft Propulsion System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: To mitigate the safety risks and increase the torque capability as well for electric aircraft propulsion system, a novel axial-flux permanent magnet vernier machine (PMVM) with H-core stator modules is proposed and analyzed in this article. The stator of this machine is totally composed of H-core modules with separate toroidal windings, which can isolate all stator modules physically and mostly prevent the propagation of faults. Besides, due to the flux modulation effect, the output torque also increases and both the output performance and safety can be guaranteed. Firstly, the machine topology and working principle are analyzed and provided, and the feasible slot/pole combinations, armature windings, gear ratio are derived and analyzed. Secondly, to fairly compare the performances of this modular axial-flux machine, a benchmark YSAS axial-flux machine is selected and designed as the comparison candidate. The comprehensive performance, such as the no-load back-EMF, inductance, output torque, losses, and efficiency et al., is simulated by finite-element analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: Metaheuristics-based Optimal Powertrain Sizing for a Hybrid Electric Passenger Ferry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A global shift toward sustainable transportation has prompted the maritime industry to lead in the electrification of water vessels. Battery electric powertrains show great promise in reducing fuel consumption and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions; however, high capital expenditures are required to deploy this technology. In other studies, the design of hybrid electric vehicles using metaheuristic algorithms has successfully minimized total costs and equivalent carbon dioxide emissions. This study developed a design methodology for a hybrid electric powertrain for inland waterway ferries, utilizing genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO), techniques that have been used in land vehicles. A hybrid electric powertrain model was used to simulate its real-life operation. An evaluation of the total cost of ownership (TCO) and lifetime carbon (CO2) emissions measured its economic feasibility and environmental impact. The study successfully exploited GA and PSO to design a hybrid electric passenger ferry, reducing up to 39.05% of TCO and 28.51% of CO2 emissions.

articleTitle: Design of LCC-S-Compensated Wireless Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor System for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In electric vehicle applications, cable components used in traditional motor drive power supply solutions are susceptible to damage and reliability issues due to continuous vibration or bending. To address these challenges, a wireless power transmission-based permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive system is proposed in this paper. It utilizes an innovative LCC-S compensation network for a steady DC-link voltage output, aiming to eliminate wired connections and enhance the flexibility and reliability of the motor drive system. Both simulation analysis and experimental results are analyzed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed system, showing a wireless transmission efficiency of 65%.

articleTitle: An Ultrasonic-assisted Nanofluid Direct Contact Liquid-based Battery Thermal Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A novel battery thermal management system (BTMS) is proposed in this work by incorporating hybrid heat transfer enhancement mechanisms, where the ultrasonic-assisted nanofluid immersion cooling metho is employed. A large number of diamond nanoparticles are suspended in the base fluid, exhibiting insulating characteristics, engages in immersion liquid cooling system with a mini-channel structure. Additionally, the application of ultrasound further intensifies the heat transfer effect. An experimental study is conducted to analyze the individual impact of various variables on temperature characteristics through the single factor analysis, including the volume flow rate, nanoparticle concentration, ultrasonic frequency and power. On this basis, the proposed system is optimized by considering multiple factors. The experimental results demonstrate that the optimized BTMS exhibits superior performance in both heat transfer efficiency and system temperature uniformity, with the maximum temperature being less than 35.2 °C, and the maximum temperature difference can be controlled within 1.6 °C.

articleTitle: Internal Short Circuit Detection in Battery Pack Based on Internal Resistance Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in various energy storage scenarios. Battery safety in energy storage systems is paramount due to its critical role in preventing incidents and ensuring reliable operation. This research focuses on the safe operation and maintenance issues in the field of lithium-ion batteries and proposes a new anomaly detection method. The existing technology mainly determines battery abnormalities and faults by directly identifying voltage signals, but there are problems such as difficulty in threshold selection, high computational complexity, and insufficient accuracy. In this article, an equivalent circuit model and an internal short circuit model are established based on the actual parameters of the battery test. Then screened the internal short circuit single cells through parameter comparison. Finally achieving online implementation, simple operation, and high-accuracy anomaly detection. The proposed method has high application potential and can provide strong support for the safety management of lithium-ion battery packs.

articleTitle: Investigation on a Constrained Adaptive Control for Dual-Motor Driving Systems Based on ABLF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Dual-motor driving systems are increasingly popular in heavy-duty transport propulsion systems in both civilian and military domains for their robust driving ability. These type of driving systems face three challenges: 1) the matched uncertainties caused by the inaccurate model parameters and the unmatched uncertainties caused by the nonlinear gear backlash; 2) rapid response and smooth operation are required simultaneously under heavy-load conditions; 3) asynchronism between the two driving motors. In this paper, an adaptive law is designed to estimate system parameters, while the matched and unmatched uncertainties of the system are estimated by two full-state feedback linear extended state observers (LESOs). Additionally, the asymmetric barrier Lyapunov function (ABLF) and the boundary function (BF) are combined by the backstepping technique to achieve rapid response within the system constraints. Furthermore, dual motors are considered as an averaged virtual motor, with compensating currents introduced to eliminate the difference between their rotational speeds. Simulation results indicate that this control scheme exhibits high precision and rapid response during position tracking operation.

articleTitle: Overcharge fault diagnosis method for lithium-ion batteries based on battery expansion characteristic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Overcharge is a major contributor to thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries. This paper provides an early detection method for overcharge faults based on battery expansion characteristics. Firstly, the overcharge triggering and performance characterization tests are designed by controllable charge cut-off voltage at 25 °C and 55 °C. Secondly, the lithium and active materials loss mode evolution of fault batteries under mechanical stress conditions and the impact of faults on battery performance are investigated. Additionally, the influence of battery expansion characteristics on different cut-off voltages and the correlation between differential voltage and expansion are analyzed. The results show two peaks on differential voltage and expansion occur after overcharging at 4.7 V at 25 °C. This results in a serious loss of lithium-ion and cathode-active materials. Battery expansion shifts from contraction to sustained expansion during the rest of the process after overcharging, which is attributed to gas generation caused by electrolyte decomposition, especially for high temperatures.

articleTitle: Megawatt-Level Charging for Mining Trucks: Operational Demonstration and Effectiveness Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: As an advanced technology in the field of heavy-duty electric transportation, megawatt-level charging technology is gradually becoming a key solution to the bottlenecks faced by traditional charging methods. With the global mining sector accelerating its transition to green and low-carbon practices, electric mining trucks exhibit great potential in terms of carbon reduction and operational economics. However, traditional charging technologies, due to their long recharging times and low efficiency, cannot fully meet the demands of mining trucks in high-intensity work environments. Therefore, there is an urgent need for the research and application of megawatt-level fast charging technology.This paper, based on the actual operational conditions of the Ordos mining demonstration in Inner Mongolia, calculates the total lifecycle economics of megawatt-level charging mining trucks, analyzing the economic differences between these and fuel mining trucks in terms of investment, time, and fuel costs. It conducts simulations and economic calculations for the scaled-up operation of mining truck fleets, considering the changes in investment and operating costs for megawatt-level charging mining trucks after large-scale development. Furthermore, it provides relevant recommendations for the operation of megawatt-level charging mining trucks in the demonstration mining site.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Fault Diagnosis for Sensors in Commercial Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell System Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Reliability and safety are two key concerns for proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) vehicles, but the potential consequences caused by sensor failures pose significant threats to these aspects, especially in commercial vehicles that are more cost-sensitive. This article introduces a novel sensor fault diagnosis approach for PEMFCs based on a data-driven method. The method employs multi-signal data-image conversion and reconstruction to cope with situations where sensor data are highly coupled and difficult for dimensional reduction. Transfer learning (TL) is also implemented, using pre-trained Inception v1 as the knowledge for TL in sensor fault diagnosis, based on the dataset collected from real road operations of commercial fuel cell tractors. The proposed TL-Inception identifies six fault types with an accuracy rate of up to 98.29%, outperforming other common methods, particularly in missed diagnosis, indicating its high sensitivity. Moreover, the method demonstrates sensitivity to fault characteristics in discrete and continuous sliding time windows and shows the potential for multi-fault diagnosis and time-varying response capability.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of the Anti-Interturn Short-circuit Fault High-Speed Permanent Magnet Starter Generator for Aviation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The interturn short-circuit (ITSC) fault, being a frequently occurring issue, often leads to a significant ITSC current in the high-speed permanent-magnet starter generator (HSPMSG), thereby limiting their application to industries with strict reliability requirements, such as aviation. Moreover, the tolerance of ITSC faults typically contradicts power density. This paper conducted a multi-objective optimization design of HSPMSG to achieve a balance between power density and ITSC current, ensuring the possibility of long-term operation under ITSC fault while maintaining competitive power density. Firstly, the key parameters that affect ITSC current and power density were selected as the optimized variables, and then the multi-physics field constraints were studied. Subsequently, an optimized design process was developed and implemented. Finally, the optimal scheme was confirmed considering its performance and technological feasibility. The research will facilitate the rapid utilization of HSPMSGs in aviation power generation systems.

articleTitle: Research on Control Methods for Electric Vehicle Networks Based on FlexRay Bus
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: With the rapid development of electric, intelligent, and connected vehicles, the demand for onboard network technology in vehicles is increasing. The timeliness and robustness of onboard network technology have become key influencing factors for electric vehicle performance. CAN bus cannot meet the high-speed communication requirements of electric vehicles, while FlexRay bus become the preferred solution for intelligent development of electric vehicles due to its high bandwidth, reliability, determinism. This paper analyzes the, topology structure, and timeliness of Flex onboard network system. It also conducts in-depth research on the communication mechanism of FlexRay protocol and designs a FlexRay bus control suitable for data communication between complex onboard electronic control (ECUs). The design covers basic concepts of the FlexRay bus protocol, core transmission processes, data frame formats, encodingdecoding methods as well as implementation and simulation of multiple transmission modules. The functionality of transmission modules is simulated to complete the construction and design of the overall structure of the FlexRay controller. Finally, functional simulation and verification are performed on the designed FlexRay bus controller The test results show that this FlexRay bus controller performs well in terms of data transfer, real-time capability, and robustness; it can meet the requirements for onboard network technology electric vehicles.

articleTitle: A deep learning-based parameter identification approach of electrochemical impedance spectrum equivalent model for lithium-ion batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is a power technique in battery research that includes kinetics characteristic analysis, degradation mechanism, and state estimation and prediction. The impedance model is usually employed to analyze battery EIS quantitatively, and parameter identification for the impedance model is of vital importance. However, the current parameter identification for the impedance model is mainly achieved through heuristic optimization and nonlinear least squares methods, which may be time consuming when used to process a large amount of EIS data at once with low convergence speed. To deal with these issues, this study proposes an innovative parameter identification method for the battery impedance model using the Neural Network approach. First, the relationship between cyclic aging and model parameter variation was investigated. To enhance the networks' adaptiveness and effectiveness, 32000 synthetic EISs were generated to assist the offline training process. Then four Neural Network models with EIS data within different frequency ranges as input were employed to identify the model parameters. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method can achieve a relative mean absolute error of 2.30% compared with software RelaxIS, and a mean error impedance 3.64E–4 Ohm compared to experimental EIS.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Online Energy Management for Fuel Cell Vehicles with Improved Speed Prediction Using Variational Mode Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Effective energy management is essential for the optimal control of fuel cell vehicles. This paper aims to reduce fuel consumption and decrease degradation of the fuel cell system for fuel cell vehicles through multi-objective online energy management. Firstly, the traditional vehicle speed prediction model is improved using the variational mode decomposition method to enhance accuracy. Then, based on the predicted vehicle speed, driving conditions including speed and acceleration are obtained. Subsequently, fuzzy logic control is used to adaptively adjust the equivalent factor of the traditional equivalent consumption minimization strategy based on the driving conditions and battery's state of charge, forming an advanced multi-objective online energy management strategy. Simulation results verify the superior performance of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: State of Charge Estimation Based on Physical Information Neural Network Parameter Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Accurate estimation of the State of Charge (SoC) is not only an important reference for calculating the driving range of electric vehicles but also a key technical support forfault detection in lithium-ion batteries. In this paper, we propose a physical information neural network that utilizes the differential state equation and the output state equation of the second-order RC model to identify the internal parameters of the model. Additionally, we incorporate a multi-head attention mechanism to effectively integrate temporal information within the input data. Then, the derived model parameters and measured data were fed into the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) neural network to estimate the State of Charge (SoC). We verify the effectiveness of the proposed method through experimental simulation and comparison with other methods.

articleTitle: Competitive Pricing of Electric Vehicle Charging in Coupled Power and Transportation Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The increasing penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) is coupling the power and transportation networks. The charging price set by the charge service provider plays a crucial role in guiding the routing and charging choices of EVs, which further affects the operation of coupled power and transportation networks. In this paper, we explore the pricing problem from the perspective of self-interested charge service providers. We adopt the mixed-user equilibrium model with elastic traffic demands to model the transportation network. The power distribution network is described as an optimal power flow model, which is relaxed into a second-order cone programming. We then propose a path generation algorithm to describe the routing and charging choices of EVs in the coupled network based on the Dijkstra method to avoid path enumeration. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. It proves that price competition between charge service providers can help balance the benefit of transportation network, power distribution network, and drivers.

articleTitle: Revealing the relationship between external pressure and lithium plating of pouch lithium-ion batteries based on in-situ impedance and relaxation voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Lithium plating during fast charging poses a significant threat to battery lifespan and safety. However, conventional lithium plating detection methods relying on specialized equipment fail to meet the practical demands of fast charging technology development. Novel approaches are required to overcome these limitations. Relevant studies indicate a strong correlation between the mechanical characteristics of batteries and lithium plating. This study, leveraging relaxation voltage and in-situ impedance measurements, revealed the relationship between force characteristics and lithium plating. The results indicate that the differential force curve can be used to characterize the onset of lithium plating. In the absence of lithium plating, the differential force plot does not exhibit a prominent second peak. By comparison, if lithium plating occurs, the second peak will be relatively pronounced, which corresponds to the onset of lithium plating. The proposed online lithium plating diagnosis method based on differential force detection, which can be integrated into the current battery management system (BMS), enables dynamic adjustment of the charging current. By detecting the onset of lithium plating and identifying its initial stage, the BMS can take proactive measures to suppress its further progression.

articleTitle: A Topology Identification and Calibration Method Based on Structural Equation Modeling in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Distribution network topology identification and calibration are essential to ensure the supply reliability and advanced application of distribution system, such as power flow analysis, state estimation, fault location, etc. However, the lack of measurement equipment, frequent changes in distribution system topology, and high-penetration renewable energy sources make distribution network topology identification become a challenging problem in practical. In this paper, the structural equation modeling (SEM) in distribution networks is introduced to relate the nodes and branches of the distribution network. The proposed method uses measurements from multiple phasor measurement units (PMUs) and pseudo-measurements of injected power at nodes to estimate the distribution network topology and check the accuracy by up-KVL and down-KVL calibration process. At the same time, the correlation of all the node measurements is compared to calibrate the correctness of the topological connections of the distribution network as well as the completeness of the topological objects. The effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method are verified by simulation in an IEEE 33-node system.

articleTitle: A Current-Fed Full-Bridge Boost LCL-Type DC/DC Converter With Parallel Capacitors On Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper investigates a current-fed full-bridge boost DC/AC/DC converter based on series LCL resonance. By paralleling an additional capacitor on every power switch, a wide input voltage range (50-162V) and a narrow switching frequency range (100-125kHz) are achieved. To maintain a constant output voltage, frequency control with a constant turn-off time for switches is employed, enabling Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) without the need for any auxiliary circuitry. The converter eliminates the DC bus capacitor by utilizing traditional capacitors under a resonant function. Through waveform modulation of the tank voltage, the energy dissipation is minimized. To help the design, A Fourier’s mathematical description is exploited. The operational principle, detailed mathematical analysis are given, and simulation results are presented to validate the feasibility of the proposed converter.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Two Permanent Magnet Vernier Machines With E-Core Stator Modules for Electric Aircraft Propulsion System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Electrical machines are essential components for the electric aircraft propulsion system, and both output performance and fault-tolerance are indispensable for electrical machines. In this paper, two permanent magnet vernier machines (PMVMs) with various multiple E-core stators are proposed and compared. Both stators are completely composed of E-core modules, but the phases of the conventional one are distributed circumferentially, and the counterpart of the phase-unit axial-modular machine is axially distributed, where each phase is also composed of several E-core modules. When the fault occurs in one module, this can be easily cut and replaced, which exhibits superior fault-tolerance. Firstly, the proposed modular machine topology is illustrated and summarized, and the feature of each kind is further investigated. Secondly, the two machine topologies are listed and compared in details, and the working principle is also validated by theoretical analysis. Afterwards, performance comparisons between the two modular machines are carried out, including the no-load and on-load performance, e.g., no-load back-EMF, inductance, torque characteristic, and power factor. Based on these theoretical and finite-element analysis (FEA), the characteristics of two modular machines can be then extracted. Eventually, the prototype with E-core modules were manufactured and tested to further verify the performance of two modular machines, and the experimental results have a good agreement with the analysis before.

articleTitle: A Review on the Development of Renewable Ammonia Powered Transportation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: As global attention on carbon neutrality intensifies, ammonia has emerged as a strong candidate to replace fossil fuels due to its zero carbon emissions and high energy density. This paper first defines renewable ammonia and sets the standards for its production, analyzing the Haber-Bosch process combined with renewable energy. It also examines the storage and transportation methods of ammonia. The paper then assesses the potential of ammonia as a fuel for internal combustion engines and power generation systems, with a focus on recent research developments. The study concludes that, in the short to medium term, the electrolysis-Haber process will become the mainstream technology route for renewable ammonia production, although several key technical issues need to be addressed. The trend is toward miniaturization and modularization of electrolysis-Haber process equipment to better match the characteristics of renewable energy.

articleTitle: A small sample conventional circuit breaker fault diagnosis method based on SWT-STFT and double flow CNN-SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A small sample conventional circuit breaker fault diagnosis method based on SWT-STFT and double flow CNN-SVM is proposed to address the low accuracy of model fault diagnosis caused by the complex operating conditions, insufficient vibration signal samples, strong individual sample differences, and difficulty in extracting features of conventional circuit breakers. Firstly, feature parameters are extracted during the closing period of the conventional circuit breaker using SWT-STFT to form a high-dimensional feature dataset; Use CNN to adaptively extract features from the feature dataset, and then use SVM to classify and recognize the output of CNN's fully connected layers. Use Hippo Optimization (HO) Algorithm to optimize the parameters of SVM and improve its classification performance. The results show that the SWT-STFT and double flow CNN-SVM models have higher diagnostic accuracy for small sample conventional circuit breakers compared to traditional SVM CNN methods have shown good accuracy improvement. In the testing experiment, this model can accurately diagnose mechanical faults of small sample conventional circuit breakers, providing strong support for the stable operation of the power system.

articleTitle: Diving Warning for Lithium-ion Batteries Based on Capacity Variance and Relaxation Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are commonly employed in electric vehicles due to their superior performance, however, which usually exhibit non-linear degradation behavior with knee-point where the battery capacity degrades at an accelerated rate. Therefore, it is crucial to accurately identify and predict the knee-point for battery maintenance and replacement to ensure the stabilized usage of the battery. This study firstly proposes a capacity variance-based method for both offline and online identification of battery knee-point by calculating the variance ratio of the anterior and posterior within a sliding window in real time. Additionally, variance, maximum and mean features are extracted from the discharge relaxation voltage, showing a significant linear relationship with the knee-point, with the advantage of predicting in advance. Lastly, an online battery capacity diving warning method is proposed based on the identification method and linear relationship. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is capable of providing real-time warnings of the knee-point in advance of its occurrence, with an overall mean absolute error of 13.60.

articleTitle: Construction of electrochemical model of lithium-ion battery and evaluation of electrolyte performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In recent decades, considerable research has been conducted to investigate the impact of diverse variables in lithium-ion batteries on battery performance and to enhance their functionality at the mechanistic level through simulation. As a crucial component of the electrolyte, the electrolyte salt serves the function of facilitating the transportation of lithium ions. Nevertheless, the impact of electrolyte salt concentration on the cycling performance of lithium-ion batteries and the underlying mechanism remain insufficiently understood. Consequently, this paper uncovers the impact of electrolyte salt concentration on the constant-current-voltage charging duration and the micro-mechanism by charging/discharging cycles of batteries with varying electrolyte salt concentrations, establishing a one-dimensional electrochemical simulation model. The findings offer promising insights for determining the optimal range of electrolyte salt concentration to enhance the cycling performance of lithium-ion batteries.

articleTitle: A Review on the Development of Renewable Hydrogen Powered Transportation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper synthesizes the various definitions of renewable provided by globally recognized organizations to establish a unified understanding. It subsequently conducts a comprehensive review of the industrial and technological advancements throughout the renewable hydrogen-powered transportation system’s value chain. The review focuses on five critical domains: Renewable Hydrogen Production, Storage- Transportation-Refueling Infrastructure, Vehicle Powertrain Technology, Transportation Equipment, and Operational Models. Scalable production of renewable hydrogen faces significant challenges, despite the long-standing history of the electrolysis equipment industry. The high-pressure gaseous hydrogen storage, transportation, and refueling system for road transportation is currently in a promotional phase, whereas other methods of hydrogen storage and transportation remain in early development stages. The use of ammonia and methanol as hydrogen carriers holds promise in the short to medium term. Hydrogen powertrain technology is largely centered around fuel cells, with hydrogen- powered vehicles predominantly used in heavy-duty applications in remote areas rich in renewable energy and with weak power grids. The gaseous nature of hydrogen leads to substantial differences in transportation equipment, storage, transportation, and refueling infrastructure, as well as operational models, when compared to conventional gasoline and diesel systems, resulting in higher capital and operational expenses.

articleTitle: Multi-time Scale Probabilistic Aggregation Technology of Large-scale Electric Vehicle Energy Storage Batteries Participating in Grid Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: With the rapid development of electric vehicles (EVs), aggregators can use reliable technology to aggregate widely distributed lithium batteries, enabling deterministic centralized output and effectively participating in multi-time scale grid demand response, thereby achieving significant economic benefits. This paper analyzes demand response across different time scales, such as minutes and hours, and studies the multi-time matching technology of probabilistic profiling techniques. The SOM neural network clustering method is used to aggregate EV loads, and aggregators control the unified charging and discharging behavior of EV batteries. A mixed-integer linear programming optimization algorithm is employed to allocate the aggregated battery resources, ensuring optimal energy distribution. Finally, simulations based on typical daily EV random operation scenarios show an improvement in the revenue and operational satisfaction of EV aggregators, validating the effectiveness of the aggregation technology.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Centralized and Distributed BMS Topologies for LEV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a techno-economic analysis and comparison of two battery management system (BMS) topologies namely centralized BMS (CBMS) and distributed BMS (DBMS). Testing, characterization, and analysis were constrained within light electric vehicle (LEV) applications that operate at extra-low voltage DC (≤120VDC). High energy LiFePO4 battery packs were used to test and characterize the two BMS topologies in terms of flexibility and expandability, installation complexity, fault tolerance, redundancy, communications implementation, and battery equalization performance. The DBMS topology excels in terms of flexibility and expandability, fault tolerance, redundancy, and charge equalization. The CBMS, with its straightforward implementation is more practical when it comes to ease of installation and simplicity of communication protocol. In terms of cost, the DBMS technology used in this paper is the more cost-effective solution in comparison to the CBMS topology.

articleTitle: An Early Remaining Useful Life Prediction Method for Lithium-ion Batteries using Optimization Algorithm-Assisted Gaussian Process Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used as power devices for electric vehicles due to their high energy density and fast charging capability. However, battery life degradation adversely affects safety management and utilization maintenance. Therefore, research on battery life prediction can help early health diagnosis and residual value assessment to prevent system downtime. Aiming at the problems of poor early prediction ability of current methods, this paper proposes an early life prediction method for lithium-ion batteries using optimization algorithm-assisted Gaussian Process Regression. Firstly, six health features strongly correlated with end-of-life are extracted from the battery's first 100 cycles of charge/discharge data. Then, a battery life prediction model is established based on Gaussian Process Regression with composite kernel functions. The particle swarm optimization algorithm is employed to optimize the hyperparameters of the composite kernel functions, enhancing the adaptiveness of the proposed prediction method. The validation result shows that the prediction is highly accurate, and the mean absolute percentage error of early life prediction can reach 10.66% overall. The Gaussian Process Regression model based on hyperparameter optimization proposed in this paper has better prediction accuracy compared with the prediction results without hyperparameter tuning and with a single kernel function. The method proposed in this paper also outperforms other common machine learning algorithms in terms of prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Standardization Framework and Policy Recommendation of the Electric Propulsion System of an Electric Passenger Ferry for Inland Waterways in the Philippines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Aligned with the 10-year Marina Industry Development Plan (MIDP) aimed to enhance the Philippine marine industry from 2019 to 2028, the agency released nine new and revised domestic shipping circulars, and policies. Additionally, they issued Philippine Ship Safety Rules and Regulations (PSSRR) for passenger ships Part B (less than 500 GT), focusing on designing and constructing the superstructure of such vessels, including those for inland waterways. Despite these efforts and the International Maritime Organization's goal to achieve net-zero GHG emissions by 2050, no available references have been used to standardize marine electric propulsion components in the Philippines. This research develops a standardization framework for the electric propulsion system of an electric passenger ferry for inland waterways that can be adopted in the Philippines. Relevant standards from the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) were reviewed to identify the gaps between existing local standards and policies. The paper presented a method for incorporating these standards in electric ferry design and evaluated three sets of commercially available electric propulsion systems for compliance with IEC standards in preparation for a local electric ferry design. The findings will aid the local maritime industry in identifying necessary standards for adopting and transitioning to fully electric passenger ferries.

articleTitle: Pricing Strategy for Charging Operators with Both Fixed and Mobile Charging Facilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: With the development of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, a novel charging facility characterized by mobility and modularity arises. In this paper, we propose a pricing and charger component deployment strategy for the charging operators, who hold both mobile and fixed charging facilities. We take into account the price elasticity, the impact of charger number, the EV user’s choice of charging station, and the competitive relationship with other operators. An algorithm based on particle swarm optimization is proposed to solve the optimal pricing and charger components distribution model for each operator, and then an evolutionary game is used to describe the process of competitively adjusting the operators’ strategies. Case study results verify the validity of the proposed model and method.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging Guidance Strategy Based on Hierarchical Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: To address effectively the stochastic charging demand of electric vehicles, this paper proposes a charging guidance strategy for electric vehicles based on hierarchical multi-agent deep reinforcement learning. This strategy refines the charging guidance task into a double-layer finite Markov decision process for the complex feature information in the coupled system of electric vehicles, charging stations, and transportation networks. In this architecture, the upper network adopts a centralized learning and decentralized execution strategy, and each electric vehicle is regarded as an independent agent. These agents cooperate in diverse incentives and competitive environments to jointly recommend the best charging station locations. At the same time, the action decision outputs of the upper network are integrated into the state considerations of the lower multi-agents. The lower network adopts the same solution method as the upper network, and the lower multi-agent plans the optimal driving paths based on the latest EV and traffic network states after receiving the upper decision. Further, a multi-agent hybrid Q learning algorithm is introduced to solve the problem, and constraints are imposed on the agent rewards to guide the multi-agent learning. Finally, simulation results validate that the proposed strategy enhances electric vehicle charging efficiency and promotes efficient road network operation.

articleTitle: Influence of Specimen Selection on Lifetime Prediction of Low Voltage Electrical Machines Under Variable Temperature Aging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: To a great extent, electric machine (EM) lifetime is affected by electrical failures that compromise the integrity of the windings electrical insulation system (EIS). During EMs operation, the EIS suffered various stresses, such as, thermal, electrical, mechanical and ambient (TEAM), which lead the deterioration and decrease the dielectric property of EIS.
